column1: # INTERACTIONS -- who was in the room, and what happened. Append-only.
# *** THIS IS THE FILE THE CAMPAIGN HAS BEEN MISSING. ***
# Social events lived ONLY in prose -- three thousand lines of it -- which is
# why "narrating from my own summary instead of from the log" is the largest
# error class in this campaign. Every one of these was a query that could not be
# run:
#   how Kell died          ..  narrated backwards
#   Sim's two years        ..  wrong
#   Cuddy toward Yrtone    ..  called cold; npcs.md said the opposite
#   Ista's grievance       ..  extended to a cart trip it never covered
#   the barrel "never moved" .. world_changes.tsv:419 says otherwise
#   "the plan was the 51st" .. the DM's own calendar row, read back as theirs
#   Meg and Tibb           ..  a mother and her grown son, written as two families
#   "you nearly forgot Wend" .. they had been the ones reminding him
# `people` is a COMMA LIST on purpose: it has to be typeable at the table. The
# build normalises it into a proper join, and the validator REFUSES any name
# that does not resolve to campaign/people.tsv -- so "Wetherby", "Rell's
# brother" and a typo are all caught at the moment of writing.
# `seq` numbers the scenes within a day, so `evidence` elsewhere can point at
# "77:3" and mean something exact.
# `kind`: first_contact | counsel | negotiation | promise | payment | grievance
#         | teaching | report | conflict | fact
#   `fact` is for a dated thing that is true of somebody and will stop being
#   true -- "Cuddy is frail" -- which is an EVENT, not a property, and filing it
#   as a property is how Ancel's "Unanswered" outlived its answer by 43 days.
# `reaction` is the d100 where one was rolled. MOST OF THE TIME THERE IS NONE:
# DMG p.63 is a FIRST-CONTACT mechanic and rolling it at friends was itself one
# of the errors (four times in one hour). Blank means no roll, deliberately.
# SEEDED 2026-09-11 from campaign/sessions/. Not every scene -- the ones a query
# would be run against: first contacts, the reactions, the promises, and the
# findings. `evidence` points at the session file, which is verbatim and
# complete.
day
column8: summary
THE SURETY. Dave answerable for Hask, Dellie, Corm and Sarn by name and aloud. Nothing on paper either way; the condition is that the four must be visibly WORKING
Met on the road, half-day 1 of the patrol. Neutral until Dave named Ottir. Had driven the whole lonely stretch and seen nothing, and TOLD THE MARKET SO UNPROMPTED, naming the party
NOT DOWN THE HOLE -- I'll not ask that of anybody who isn't paid to take that kind of risk. Dave will not ask any hired man into the caves. A promise, not a preference
WEND COMES ROUND BEFORE ANYONE SPOKE -- not for the money and not for the argument, but because they walked the road publicly for six days. "I got it from watching"
Coll's standing instruction: bring in anyone desperate and put them to work. "If people need work I trust your judgement." He did exactly that and wrote down what each was owed
Marrow asked DAVE to ask his son what he wanted, because he could not. "I suppose I thought if he said he wanted to stay, I'd have to let him"

Reaction 11, BADLY FRIGHTENED -- pulled to 81 when Dave took his mail off in the road where the crossbowman could watch. Came north TO BUY, on a rumour. Asked Osk who to speak to about next summer's wool
WEND TAKES THE FACTORSHIP. Her price is the succession document: two years, then she spends it on the town as she sees fit
Dave quoted Sim to his father word for word. Marrow asked the boy directly for the first time in two years and got his "Aye." THE THREAD CLOSES

*** THE ANSWER TO ANCEL'S QUESTION, TWO DAYS AFTER HE ASKED IT. *** He cannot buy the clip and says so, then names FOUR BUYERS who do not know Wethersby exists -- two raw-wool men east of Marchford, a FULLER WHO TAKES CLOTH, and a factor's man. A penny in the pound for three years; he asked two and Wend haggled him up
Brokered by Wend. Marrow made him say the four names twice, then where they were and what they bought. Marrow bought him his dinner
GYLL PAYS RESTITUTION TO THE ELEVEN, 4 gp 10 sp apiece, selling the grey mare to cover the shortfall, SAID ALOUD IN THE SQUARE with Ottir witnessing
The leg mends clean and he will not limp. HE CANNOT READ AND HE ASKED TO LEARN
The buyer of last resort agreed -- 8 gp the tod, cap 500 the season. She needs a CLERK and DOES NOT KNOW SARN HAS BEEN KEEPING THE TALLY
THE SURETY IS SATISFIED. Wace has written: the account of the hundred at Draycot on day 52. Ottir asked the one hard question about Quasqueton -- whose is it?
*** HALM'S STANDING WANT, asked once and never again: "One load's a load. What I'd want, someday, is a RUN. Osk's got a run. He knows where he is on a Tuesday." ***
Met riding north. Usher of the hall, buying a bed for a spring wedding. Gave away WHY WACE WROTE, for nothing, and it defused everything
The chest gets read. He has the run of it, nobody minds an almoner reading, and ten days
THE SKELETONS TOLD AND HOLY WATER REFUSED. Cuddy is a cleric of the 3rd; DMG p.114 requires the 5th, and his chapel has no font
THE DWARF IN IRONS, told second and should have been first. "I have never once had to be told about a man forty years late." His one flat instruction: BRING HIM OUT

THE CRAG. The title cannot be settled from that chest -- but a grant NAMING ROGAHN AND ZELLIGAR, to hold of the lord FOR THE KEEPING OF THE NORTH WAY. Counsel: do not raise the title, ask for the LICENCE
THE PETITION. The licence GRANTED AS ASKED and backdated to Michaelmas last. He never read the perambulation -- d6=4, vindicating Cuddy completely
SHE FINDS THE HOLE NOBODY ELSE SAW: the licence says stone and timber, and it is not a bill of sale for a dead wizard's balances
THE DOUBLE BIND, CALLED OUT AND DISSOLVED. "Let me spend it" read as asking permission that was not the party's to give. The rule that came out of it is about POWER, NOT PHRASING
THE MESSAGE TO ISTA WENT BADLY
He finds the SAME hole four hours later -- corroboration, not coincidence. AND HE FINDS THE TRICK: ask for nothing substantive, then ask for A RECEIPT, because a receipt recites what the letter said

Why's the glass smoked? Somebody paid extra so this could sit in the dark. THE VIAL IS REALGAR -- a pigment, poisonous, degrades in light. He opened it himself in shade with a wet rag, everyone else eight feet back
The realgar sold for 35 gp

THE DYE AT COST, AND THE FIRST FINDING RUNS AGAINST THE PARTY. At cost is a discount and a discount is a gift wearing a trade's clothes -- and then Dave put a FIGURE on it and it went to 5. "Thirty years telling people what's in a jar for nothing and nobody's ever costed it"
HASK SELLS THE SMALL GOODS AND DOES NOT UNDERSELL, holding his number through two silences. 160 gp. THE LINE CLOSES: 573 on 357
FATHER DOULE IS FIFTH LEVEL -- Cuddy's lead was good -- AND MARCHFORD HAS NO FONT. "I can make it. I have never made it." The priest and the vessel are in different towns
Dill is the missing link in the party's own cloth chain, and he is a DRESSER, not a labourer
He holds to his terms exactly. 31 gp at his door; 18 owing in three quarterly instalments

ELEVEN SHILLINGS LENT TO DILL for his tools -- and he asked for it to be written as a DEBT, repayable out of his first month, rather than taken as a gift. articles.md's first finding running the right way round: a job cancels a debt, a gift deepens one, and he chose the form himself
PAID ~250 GP, his full valuation, the moment he was shown Wace's receipt. His day-42 condition DISCHARGED after twenty-three days. Over a thousand gold for the first time
THE LOOM IS NARROW -- and she turns it round: "It isn't one weaver too many. IT'S ONE LOOM TOO FEW." She REFUSES THE CARTS as a gift and proposes letting them at the wear
HOLT NAMES THE CASK OFF THE BUNG without tapping it -- strong stock ale, thirty years and not turned. 58 gp: 30 in coin and 28 in his own hand, written unasked
THE STRUCTURE SIGNED, articles.md art. 13. 300 gp wage reserve, cash, locked, NO exception clause. Fair copy in SARN'S hand, witnessed by OTTIR

*** NAN CAN GRADE WOOL. *** Nine years on Rell's ground, and she knows WHOSE -- Ellery honest, two past Wettleford roll theirs wet, Marrow's the best in the hundred, and a widow at Hobb's Lane with three years of it in a loft. "Nobody has ever asked her a single question about wool. Including me"
CUDDY IS FRAIL. The wet in his chest, seventy-odd, November. Not dying, and it did not show in September

*** A MAN HAS BEEN SENT ABOUT THE ANIMATED DEAD. *** His house did not write to ask questions -- it wrote to say a man is coming. "In thirty years I have never once had a letter that said somebody was coming"
He asks Dellie to learn the words for the dwarf -- "not today, in case" -- and teaches her for an hour at the table. "There ought to be two of us who can and not one"

THE ROOF. He does not know and will not guess -- and reframes it: "Whose is it is the wrong end of it. They ask WHO MENDED IT LAST, and who paid the man." PERRIN STRUCK OFF because he refers upward. He will not carry it himself
NO AMOUNTS, and she owns it: "You asked me for a list and I gave you a list. A LIST ISN'T AN ORDER." It does not fit one cart. The loom goes to BERN. One addition: flax seed
The Draycot almonry account: 10 gp a year on Wend's books IN HIS NAME, a sum he DRAWS and renders. Not a purse across a table

*** THE CARRIAGE GAP. *** She had already found it and had not raised it. Carriage follows WEIGHT: the iron was 14% of the Ludbury load's value and 51% of its weight, so "at cost" was 50-70 gp BELOW cost. On Osk she has NO VIEW AT ALL and says so, naming Halm and the trap in the same breath: ask what is DONE

THE TWO CLOCKS, ruled 2026-09-11 on the player's question. Gyll's "I've had two year to find something else to say" is NOT a slip: his eleven were turned off TWO YEARS AGO when the wool staple moved and Rell died, while the road only went bad weeks before day 1. district.md already said it -- "the robberies are DOWNSTREAM... all the same event, MONTHS APART." Hask has robbed roads for twenty-two years and had never worked THIS one until a week before the party met him, so he was never one of Rell's eleven

BOTH HALVES OF THE LIST QUESTION ANSWERED, standing, on the way back out of town. HOW MUCH: the limit is what the CARTS CARRY, not the purse -- and no second run at the small goods, which sold 573 on 357 and then sat at half sold for a fortnight. WHOSE MONEY: art.7's 500 goes on the IRON AND SALT, which are sellable before shearing; THE LOOM COMES OUT OF THE PARTY'S OWN FUNDS, because art.7 names a loom as the thing it may not be spent on. Dave's own words: 'we're not interested in breaking the terms of the articles.' Wend can now cost the list

THE BRONZE WRESTLERS. Toller warm (d6=5). He values it at 115 gp and says so flatly -- a single good art object is the easiest thing in the world for him to place, which is exactly why his CASH-NOW OFFER IS 80 gp, SEVENTY PER CENT (d100=80, capped at 70 per the declared table), against the THIRTY-SIX per cent he offered on the small goods on day 55. He says the difference out loud: one good piece finds a buyer, volume does not. AND HE VOLUNTEERS THE JARS (d6=3) -- the forty containers of chemicals still sitting in Wend's barn for Trebb the dyer at Marchford, which he handed off entirely on day 77 and has evidently not stopped thinking about

THE LIST IS COSTED (d6=6) AND THE COSTING FOUND SOMETHING. Wend priced it against the carts rather than the purse, as instructed, and the list DOES NOT FILL THREE CARTS -- it fills about ONE AND A HALF, because the dear things are light and the heavy things are cheap. Iron, nails and salt are 600 lb for 100 gp; the reed and heddles weigh nothing; the flax seed is a sack. So the party has the better part of two carts of SPARE CAPACITY going south and nothing to put in them

OSK, AND HE PROPOSES GOING IN WITH THEM (d6=5). *** AND HE KNOWS WHY THE STANDING RUN CANNOT WORK AS ASKED (d6=6): HE RUNS FORTNIGHTLY BECAUSE WEEKLY WOULD RUN HALF EMPTY. *** He has carried Wethersby-Marchford for years, three days each way, and the route does not bear more traffic than that -- which is the answer to Halm's 'what I'd want is a RUN' and to Wend's condition of a load both ways, and neither of them could have known it. HIS PROPOSAL: his book of customers and his knowledge of who pays, their carts and their men, and TOGETHER the two loads fill a run that neither fills alone. AND ON THE WOOL (d6=5) he knows who buys CLOTH in Marchford, because he has carried it -- which is Wend's own open question from day 77

CORRECTION to scene 83:3, appended. THE PARTY DID NOT GO TO OSK AND DAVE DID NOT NEGOTIATE WITH HIM. Osk is WEND'S -- handed to her on day 80 with all three questions, the party saying it would confirm whatever she settled. Everything in 83:3 reached the party as HER REPORT of HER negotiation: that he runs fortnightly because the road will not bear weekly, that he proposes putting his customers in the party's carts, and that he can name the door cloth goes to in Marchford. *** AND THE STANDING INSTRUCTION, GIVEN HERE: WEND MAKES THE DECISIONS. The party does not relay between her and Osk, does not sit in, and does not want to be the channel. They confirm; she decides. *** The DM staged a yard scene with Osk in it and then asked the player what he wanted to say to him, which is both a room they never entered and a decision they had already given away

CONFIRMED, in one word. Wend's decision on Osk stands: NO PARTNERSHIP, and the carts hired out instead under a written flat rate the load, Osk's name on the contract with his customer and the loss his. The party did not argue, did not ask to sit in, and did not meet Osk -- which is the arrangement they set on day 80 working as intended. *** THE STANDING SHAPE IS NOW EXPLICIT: WEND DECIDES, THE PARTY CONFIRMS, AND NOBODY RELAYS ***

THE WOOL PARTY HOME, ten days out. *** 36 TODS at the published floor of 8 gp = 288 gp paid to holders *** -- more than expected (d6=6) and the reason is the mechanism working: WORD TRAVELLED AHEAD OF THEM (d6=4). The floor is chalked on a board in Wethersby and read to every holder, and holders talk. They were expected before they arrived. HASK HELD THE PRICE (d6=5) and did something nobody asked him to: HE MADE AN ARRANGEMENT FOR NEXT SEASON, unprompted, with holders who have not sheared yet. Uneventful road (d6=4). Nan graded, Tam wrote it, Halm carted, Rowe minded the beasts

HASK CANNOT REMEMBER WHICH HE SAID (d6=3) -- 'eight' or 'at least eight' -- and says so rather than guessing, which Wend takes better than a confident answer. HER HANDLING (d6=1): SHE WRITES TO ALL FOUR AND ASKS WHAT THEY UNDERSTOOD. Slow, safe, and it deliberately hands them the initiative: whatever they say they heard becomes the terms, because arguing a September promise in June is worth less than four holders who trust the board. SHE DOES NOT TAKE THE BUYING OFF HIM (d6=3) and says nothing further about it. *** THE PARTY SAID NOTHING THROUGHOUT, BY CHOICE *** -- they listened to the report and let their factor manage her own man

HASK ASKED, AND HE WANTS TO GO SOUTH (d6=1, plainly), for the plainest reason there is (d6=1): HE IS A FIGHTER AND THIS IS AN ESCORT, and he would rather be with the party than the books. He does not dress it up. WEND DOES NOT NEED HIM THIS FORTNIGHT (d6=4) -- the four letters and the cart-hire agreement are pen work and she does them alone. Asked at the table BECAUSE HE IS ONE OF DAVE'S FOUR, which is the fourth trigger; the buying itself would have been hers to assign and was not put to the party

WEND ON THE LIST AND WHERE IT IS BOUGHT (d6=3): MARCHFORD SERVES FOR THE BULK -- iron, nails, salt, flax seed -- and LUDBURY IS WANTED ONLY FOR THE REED AND HEDDLES, the half of a loom that cannot be made locally. *** AND BERN HAS ANSWERED, AND IT CHANGES THINGS (d6=6, then 6, then 6): HE HAS GONE AND FOUND OUT THAT THE JOB IS BIGGER THAN ANYBODY SAID, AND SAID SO HIMSELF. *** A narrow loom is not a frame with parts hung on it; the reed and the heddles have to be MATCHED to a sett he has not chosen, and he cannot order either until somebody decides what cloth is being woven and how fine. He has been honest about it against his own interest, exactly as Toller was on day 16 -- Wend's day-77 backing of him is vindicated and her own risk note ('he has never built one and is slower than a cart') turns out to be the wrong worry: he is not slow, he is CAREFUL

WEND SENDS TAM (d6=4). Her decision, not the party's. He writes, and the cloth question needs RECORDING rather than remembering -- which is the whole reason the venture has a man who writes. He carries her order for the iron, nails, salt and flax seed and does her buying at Marchford; the party escorts and does not transact. *** AND OSK HOLDS THE CLOTH NAME BACK (d6=1-2) *** until the cart-hire terms are settled. He offered it in her yard on the 81st as part of a partnership she refused, and he has not withdrawn the offer -- he has simply not repeated it. So TAM GOES SOUTH WITHOUT THE ONE NAME THAT WOULD ANSWER THE CLOTH QUESTION, and the reed and heddles wait behind it

ON THE NORTH ROAD, 25 MILES SOUTH OF WETHERSBY -- filed at Wethersby for want of a place id for the road itself, as day 6's road meeting was filed at crag_turning. PELL, NORTHBOUND: one of the carriers Osk hands off to, met once on day 58 going the other way. Reaction 41, ordinary and unhurried. HE WANTS NEWS OF THE ROAD NORTH (d6=2) and nothing else -- what the going is like past Wethersby, whether the crag road is passable, who is buying. *** AND THE PARTY IS NOW A THING HE WILL MENTION TO OTHERS: three carts of theirs on his road. *** That is precisely how Osk's trade works, and precisely what Wend refused a partnership in three days ago. ISTA'S COOKING LESSON FAILED (d6=2, then 2): SHE COULD NOT MAKE HERSELF HEARD AND GAVE UP -- four adults round a fire and a thirteen-year-old with CON 3 telling them how, so she stopped trying and cooked it herself, as she did alone on the Ludbury road

*** CORRECTION TO 84:1, APPENDED. THE DM INVENTED ISTA'S AGE AND BUILT A SCENE ON IT. *** He wrote 'a thirteen-year-old with CON 3' and made that the reason four adults talked over her. HER AGE IS RECORDED NOWHERE and nothing supports it: people.tsv has her as BERN'S PARTNER, and Bern is ~30. CON 3 is a CONSTITUTION SCORE, not an age -- read as frailty, frailty turned into youth, and an invented fact then reframed her relationship with Bern into something it is not. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, same dice (d6=2, then 2), no age in it: four people who all had opinions about bacon, and a woman who has always done this job ALONE and is not a talker. Blartho started doing it his way, Hask had a view, and twice she said something and the talk went on around her. She stopped trying and cooked it herself. Nobody was unkind and nobody noticed

OSSERY TAKES TOLLER'S ARRANGEMENT (d6=5), reaction 44, and AT ONCE -- a mercer who buys to sell on is precisely what a correspondent is, and Toller's six-in-six-towns is a description of the trade Ossery is already in. *** AND HE ADDS WHAT TOLLER DID NOT ASK FOR (d6=2): HE NAMES OTHER DEALERS IN OTHER TOWNS. *** The network builds itself, because a man who buys to sell on WANTS more places to sell on to -- Toller's condition ('two dealers in one town who know each other is one price') is served by dealers who are NOT in one town, and Ossery has no reason to protect a rival fifty miles away. TWO OF SIX SETTLED IN ONE MORNING: Toller and Ossery, with names toward the rest. Dave did the asking; Frython wrote it down

LUDBURY: OSSERY'S THREE NAMES ALL DECLINE (d6=2), and the reason is the party's own history here (d6=5, then 1): *** THEY ARE REMEMBERED IN THIS CITY AS SELLERS OF WOOL AND BUYERS OF GOODS -- 1,200 gp of clip sold on day 25, 1,038 gp spent on day 27 -- NOT as a house with goods to place. *** A city dealer hears 'correspondent' and asks what the party has to correspond ABOUT, and the honest answer is a dead wizard's leavings arriving by the cartload at irregular intervals. Ossery's names were good; the introduction was wrong. AND THE LESSON IS TOLLER'S OWN, ARRIVING FROM THE OTHER SIDE: a city does not need a correspondent in a market town. His six-in-six-towns wants TOWNS, and Ludbury is a CITY. WRAYE CONFIRMED (d6=5): the road east is good, three days, and THE LIBRARY WANTS A NAME -- an introduction, not a fee (d6=3). Strangers are not admitted on the strength of coin

*** THE REFRAME WORKS AND ONE OF THE THREE BITES (d6=4). *** Dave stopped offering goods and offered a ROUTE: Wethersby, the north hundred, and DRAYCOT -- a district that stopped coming to market when the wool staple moved. True, and completely different from 'we have a dead wizard's leavings'. AND WHAT THE DEALER WANTS IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE PARTY ASSUMED (d6=6, then 3): HE DOES NOT WANT TO BUY FROM THAT DISTRICT. HE WANTS ACCESS TO THE HALL ITSELF -- which is a NAME, not a good. Sir Aymer's household buys, and has bought from nobody in Ludbury since the staple moved, and a man who could put a mercer in front of Wace the steward would be worth more to him than any number of carts. THE PARTY HAS EXACTLY THAT: the licence, Ottir's surety, Wace's own receipt, and Cuddy. THIRD CORRESPONDENT SETTLED -- on a currency the party did not know it was carrying

IDENTIFICATION: THERE IS A MECHANISM AND IT IS A SPELLCASTER, NOT A SHOP (d6=3, then 6). The cost is not a fee -- IT IS THE MATERIAL COMPONENT. An identify spell eats A PEARL OF NOT LESS THAN A HUNDRED GOLD PIECES, consumed, per casting, and yields one property per segment of the caster's level. So the question at Wraye is not 'what does it cost to have this read' but *** 'WHO WILL CAST IT, AND WHOSE PEARL'. *** AND FRYTHON IS A MAGIC-USER: identify is a 1st-level magic-user spell, he does not have it -- he has sleep -- but a library that HOLDS the spell and a magic-user who could COPY it is a wholly different transaction from a stranger asking a favour. The library still wants an introduction and not coin (86:1)

*** CORRECTION TO 86:2, APPENDED. THE DM REVERSED THE PLAYER'S PITCH AND THEN NARRATED THE REVERSAL AS A REVEAL. *** The player said: 'we are one way to ACCESS PEOPLE FROM DRAYCOT WHO ARE BUYING' -- the dealer sells, Draycot buys, the party is the route. The DM then wrote a table asking 'what does he actually want?' with option 3-4 reading 'he wants a way to SELL INTO that district, not buy from it' -- WHICH IS THE PLAYER'S OWN PITCH, RESTATED AS AN UNKNOWN AND ROLLED FOR. To narrate the result he gave Dave a different pitch so the dealer could correct him, putting the player's words in the NPC's mouth as a rebuke to the party. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: Dave made the pitch the player made. It was correct, it was well judged, and IT SIMPLY WORKED. The dealer wants access to Sir Aymer's hall -- a NAME, not a good -- which is what the party offered and what it holds through the licence, Ottir's surety, Wace's receipt and Cuddy. No reveal, no correction, no party misunderstanding. THIRD CORRESPONDENT SETTLED

*** PLAYER-CAUGHT: LUDBURY IS A CITY AND WRAYE ONLY A TOWN, AND NOBODY HAD EVER ASKED HERE. *** The record says only 'Wraye, three days east, it has a library -- the only lead on the ring'; it NEVER said Ludbury could not help, and no source is recorded for the advice. The DM had been narrating 'the only lead' as though a city had been ruled out. ASKED PROPERLY, AND LUDBURY CANNOT HELP -- but for reasons, not for nothing. (1) THERE IS A MAGIC-USER HERE AND HE IS RETAINED BY THE CHURCH (d6=1, then 5, then 5): he takes no outside work, and that is a standing arrangement, not a refusal of the party. (2) PEARLS ARE NOT STOCK IN AN INLAND CITY -- the demand is entirely from casters and ONE MAN SUPPLIES THEM (d6=1, then 4). He will sell, AND HE ASKS WHAT IT IS FOR (d6=4). *** SO WRAYE IS NOT ARBITRARY: a town with a library that gathers casters is where you go BECAUSE the nearest city's one caster is spoken for. *** The party learned this by asking in the right place rather than by riding three days on a rumour

*** CORRECTION TO 86:5, APPENDED. PLAYER-CAUGHT. *** The DM wrote 'nobody had ever asked here' and built the scene on it. THEY ASKED ON THE FIRST VISIT: calendar.md, days 25-27, records in plain words 'NOBODY IN LUDBURY CAN IDENTIFY THE RING'. That finding is SIXTY DAYS OLD and Wraye was given as the lead at the time. WHAT TODAY ACTUALLY ADDED IS THE REASON, which was never known: the city's ONE magic-user is RETAINED BY THE CHURCH and takes no outside work; and PEARLS ARE NOT STOCK in an inland city -- one man supplies them to order and he asks what it is for. *** AND THE PLAYER'S OWN READING IS THE RIGHT ONE: different people, and sixty days of standing. *** On day 27 they were strangers who had just sold a clip. Today Dave is a man three Ludbury dealers have sat down with, one of whom wants an introduction to Sir Aymer's hall. The same question asked by a different man gets a fuller answer, and that is not a retcon -- it is what standing is FOR

NEOT, the magic-user retained by the church at Ludbury. FIRST CONTACT, DMG p.63 reaction 33 -- uncertain, 55% prone toward negative -- AND THE LEAN CAME UP 86 AGAINST 55, POSITIVE. The party asked for ADVICE and not service: we want a magic item identified, we have neither the spell nor the pearl, how is it done. HE ANSWERS FULLY AND FOR NOTHING (d6=1), AND THAT IS ALL HE CAN DO -- his retainer is exclusive and he does not pretend otherwise or make them ask twice. NOTE ON THE DICE: a d6=6 was rolled on a table written for a NEGATIVE manner and then VOIDED when the lean came up positive, and the correct table rolled instead

NEOT, SECOND ASK. (1) THE WRAYE LIBRARY: HE HAS NO NAME TO GIVE (d6=3) -- eleven years in one retainer is a small world and he says so plainly -- BUT HE HAS ADVICE ON HOW THE PLACE IS APPROACHED, which is the thing the party could not have worked out for itself. (2) *** HE HAS A PEARL AND IT IS HIS OWN *** (d6=6, then 2) -- bought years ago, not the church's, and HE WILL NOT TAKE MONEY FOR IT. WHAT HE WANTS (d6=1) IS TO BE TOLD WHAT THE RING TURNS OUT TO BE. That is the whole price. Eleven years of a retainer and a room with bad light, and what he wants from two strangers who asked a question properly is THE ANSWER TO IT. *** THE PARTY NOW OWES A DEBT THAT IS NOT MONEY AND CANNOT BE DISCHARGED AT A COUNTER -- and it is owed to a man they will have to come back to Ludbury to pay ***

DAVE PROMISES MORE THAN WAS ASKED: 'We'll come back THROUGH and tell you, and we'll give you THE STORY of how we got it too.' *** AND NEOT IS EMBARRASSED AND DEFLECTS (d6=2). *** He asked for one small thing with difficulty, having not asked anybody for anything in a long time, and being offered double it he does not know where to put himself -- says something about not wanting to keep them, and is already turning back to the table before they are out of the room. HE DOES NOT REFUSE IT. He simply cannot be thanked, which is a different thing, and the party will have to come back to find out whether he meant it

*** THE FORTY JARS, NAMED. *** Trebb reaction 46, neutral, and it does not matter -- he names them for nothing as he named the vial on day 59, because thirty years of telling people what is in a jar has never once been costed. ROLLED ON B1'S OWN d20 TABLE (module text, area 8: 'chemical compounds and supplies of NO PARTICULAR VALUE', forty containers): 5 tree sap, 4 fungus powder, 4 sand, 3 crushed stone, 3 oil, 3 vinegar, 2 each bone powder/carbon/dung/herbs/metal filings/salt/water, 1 each blood/insect bodies/spice/sulphur. *** TWENTY-SEVEN OF THE FORTY ARE A DYER'S MATERIALS *** -- metal filings and vinegar and sulphur and salt are MORDANTS, fungus powder and herbs and tree sap are COLOUR, dung is the ammonia every fuller and dyer needs. The insect bodies are a dyestuff and an ordinary one (d6=3). SHE ASKS ABOUT BRAND AND ORM BEFORE SHE ASKS ANYTHING ELSE (d6=6) and she asks it properly -- not are they trustworthy but WHO STANDS FOR THEM, which is the exact question Ottir answered for nine strangers on day 6 and the only reason any of this party has a licence, a board or a name. She does not object to them; she wants to know what she is to say when somebody asks her. THE CARTS (d6=6, both committed; d6=2, and the commitment is the light end): BOTH ARE PROMISED FOR THE DAY-100 MARKET, which is the weekly one and four days off -- board stock down from the barn and the carts standing at the board, which is what the board IS. She does not say no and she does not say yes: they are the party's own property, she has given her word on them, and she puts the two facts side by side and leaves it there. *** HER OWN LINE: back in the barn by the night of the 99th and nothing is broken. *** AND SHE ASKS WHAT THEY ARE FOR, which the party has not yet told her -- she knows nothing of the gnomes, the iron, or 421 lb under a lean-to. L047 (d6=3): FOUR DAYS ON IT AND SHE HAS A DESCRIPTION AND NO NAME -- a man on a good horse who is not a carter, who asked after WEIGHTS and wrote the answers in a book, and who has been on the southern road twice. She says the description is worth more than a name would be, because it tells her what he was doing.

*** CORRECTION TO SCENE 96:2, APPENDED NOT REWRITTEN -- PLAYER-CAUGHT, AND THE DM'S OWN ROLL ALREADY SAID SO. *** The d6 on the 96th came up 2, declared as 'the board stock alone, EASILY MOVED', and the DM then narrated both carts standing at the board all morning, which is the heavy end of a roll that landed on the light end. The player put the knife in exactly the right place: THE BARN AND THE MARKET ARE BOTH IN WETHERSBY. A cart that only has to cross a market town can make the trip four times before noon, so 'both carts, all day' was never what the commitment cost. RE-ROLLED HONESTLY (d6=4): ONE CART WORKING ALL MORNING, several trips, and that is the whole of it. *** SO BOTH CARTS CAN GO NORTH AND WEND'S WORD IS STILL GOOD, provided one is back by the night of the 99th. *** AND THE OTHER HALF THE PLAYER SUPPLIED: THERE IS A THIRD CART IN THIS TOWN. HALM has one, is in Wethersby and free on the 100th (d6=5), and has had a standing want since day 40 -- 'one load's a load' -- asked ONCE, with the man saying plainly he would not ask twice. Fifty-six days later nobody has come back to him. That is not a solution the DM handed over; it was sitting in people.tsv and in L039/L040 the whole time.

*** DAVE TELLS WEND EVERYTHING: THE CAVES, THE GNOME, THE BARGAIN, THE STORES AND THE CARTS. *** She hears the whole of expedition 11 -- 421 lb under a lean-to, 28 bars down a shaft, a gnome called Durnhak, half of what it makes, a quarter at the hole, the 101st at a watercourse. BRAND AND ORM FIRST (d6=6, and it lands BETTER THAN WHAT SHE ASKED FOR): Dave's answer is 'we agreed to show them the caves and have them come with us, that is the extent of our arrangement, and I think they can stand for themselves as they see fit.' *** SHE ASKED WHAT SHE WAS TO SAY AND HE GAVE HER A SENTENCE THAT IS SHORT, TRUE AND LIMITED, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT A FACTOR WANTS AND ALMOST NEVER GETS. *** Her own gloss: a surety is a thing you offer, not a thing you impose, and the party declining to stand for two grown men is not coldness -- it is the difference between Ottir's surety, which those nine ASKED for, and a claim made over somebody's head. WHAT SHE PICKS AT IN THE BARGAIN (d6=3): *** NOTHING IS WRITTEN DOWN. *** The whole arrangement lives in one elf's head and one gnome's, in a language nobody else in the party speaks, with no paper and no third party. Her day-54 line, unchanged: the paper is what is left when the conversation is not. AND SHE CONNECTS IT TO THE LICENCE UNPROMPTED: gnome iron and dead men's cookware are both MOVABLE GOODS OUT OF A STRONGHOLD, which is precisely what Wace's licence to quarry stone and take timber does NOT cover -- so both go in the Michaelmas letter, with the money, asking for nothing. THE KITCHEN IRON (d6=4): she has a real view and it is that it should not be weighed. Pots and pans sold singly to households beat scrap by a wide margin and the large cast-iron kettle is a wanted thing in its own right. THE CARTS ARE SETTLED: both go north in the morning.

*** DAVE PUSHES BACK AND HE IS RIGHT ON EVERY FACT. *** 'We trust you to run the business; consider trusting us on the crag.' And the record backs him completely, art.11: told Wace in the hall on the 52nd and HE WROTE IT DOWN AS THEY SAID IT; the account SENT on the 55th, signed by Dave, carried by Wat on the 56th, declaring the ~450 gp of movables by name -- pewter, books, a stone weight, garments, brass and copper instruments, glass, coin and a ring -- plus the disarming volunteered line 'of stone we have quarried none, and of timber we have taken none'; AND THE RECEIPT CAME AND RECITED THE CONTENTS (d6=5), closing it on the 65th with the steward's own hand on the lot. WEND HAD THAT RECEIPT. So her 'there's a worse one and you haven't seen it' was wrong and she takes it back. *** SHE CONCEDES THE FACT AND HOLDS THE PRINCIPLE (d6=4): the 450 is papered, the NEW goods are not, and the next account is the fix -- which Dave had already agreed to before she said it. *** AND THEN SHE RAISES THE ONE TRUE THING (d6=6), flatly, once, and NOT as a grievance: THE DAY-55 LETTER WAS DRAFTED AT TOLLER'S SHOP AGAINST HER STATED ADVICE ON TIMING AND NOBODY SHOWED IT TO HER BEFORE IT WENT. She is the factor, the custodian of the money, and the person who FOUND the hole on the 54th; the document that filled it went south without her reading a word of it, and Toller did not raise it. She only ever saw the receipt. *** HER POINT IS NOT THAT SHE WAS SLIGHTED -- IT IS THAT DAVE HAS JUST ASKED HER FOR EXACTLY THE THING THAT WAS NOT GIVEN TO HER. *** art.11's own warning box recorded this on the day as 'a fact, not a criticism'; forty-one days later it is the answer to a question nobody expected it to be asked.

*** DAVE CLOSES IT AND GIVES HER MORE THAN SHE ASKED FOR. *** 'Fair enough -- you'll see the next one first, or we'll have you there with us when we write it.' She asked for nothing; she raised the day-55 letter once and said she would leave it, and she did. THE OFFER IS THE SECOND HALF OF HER OWN DAY-54 POINT: the paper is what is left when the conversation is not, and now the person who found that hole is inside the drafting of the paper that fills it. Note WHICH thing was conceded -- not an apology, a PROCEDURE, which is the only kind of concession that survives a change of who is in the room. *** AND IT IS THE THIRD PROCEDURAL FIX IN ONE EVENING: the Brand-and-Orm sentence she now says when asked, the next Michaelmas account, and Wend in the room when it is written. *** Art. 11's warning box can be answered rather than merely standing.

*** ROWE COMES, AND HE TREATS IT AS HIS JOB RATHER THAN AS AN ADVENTURE (d6=4). *** Asked in the barn while the carts were being got ready. He minds the beasts; the beasts are going north; he goes with them. He does not ask what is at the other end and he does not ask for more money -- which is the same shape as his first appearance on day 60, where he offered that he cannot read as a DISQUALIFICATION and asked for nothing. *** THE PARTY HAS NEVER HAD A MAN WHOSE JOB IS THE ANIMALS ON A CART TRIP; every previous run was driven by whoever was free. *** THE CARTS AND MULES ARE SOUND (d6=1) -- nothing wrong, nothing he has been waiting to tell somebody, no galled shoulder or split wheel after forty idle days and the southern run. He checks the harness in front of Dave anyway, because that is what the check is for.

*** MUND THE SMITH, MET FOR THE FIRST TIME ON DAY NINETY-SEVEN. *** Reaction 52, DMG p.63: NEUTRAL -- uninterested -- uncertain, which is exactly right for a tradesman behind a counter who has been asked for two hundred spikes by people he has never served. *** AND THE REASON THEY HAVE NEVER MET HIM IS THE WHOLE SHAPE OF THIS DISTRICT: the party IMPORTS the hundred's iron on its own carts from Ludbury and sells it off the at-cost board, so in ninety-six days it has never once needed to buy worked iron in its own town. *** HE HAS THE LOT (d6=5) -- 200 spikes and 20 lb of big timber nails out of stock, no forging, no waiting. He weighs the nails in front of them, counts spikes into a sack by tens, and takes 12 gp without comment. HE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHERE HIS BAR CAME FROM (d6=2) and nobody asks him. No warmth and no suspicion; a man selling ironmongery to strangers with money.

*** BRAND AND ORM GET STRENGTH SCORES, the first time either has been load-bearing. Straight 3d6, no NPC-fighter thumb on the scale. *** BRAND 9 -- 'normal, no penalty' on STRENGTH TABLE II, so his bands are the bare 350/700/1,050. ORM 11 -- also normal, same bands. *** SO 'BIG BARE-ARMED FIGHTING MAN' IS FRAME AND REACH AND NOT EXCEPTIONAL STRENGTH, and the consequence is immediate: DAVE AT 18/26 (+1,000 to every band) IS NOT MERELY THE STRONGEST MAN ON THIS LEVEL, HE IS STRONGER THAN ANY TWO OTHERS PUT TOGETHER AT THE SAME BAND. *** Orm's day-95 'I'll carry' and picking up seventy feet of chain unasked was WILLINGNESS AND NOT STRENGTH, which is a better thing to have learned about him than the opposite. Rolled because the 1,800 gp-weight kettle had to be got out of area 2 and somebody has to be under it; the numbers were needed before the plan, not after.

*** ASKED IF THEY WANT TO COME AND LOOK FOR THE WATERCOURSE: NO (d6=1) -- AND THEN THEY ASK FOR SOMETHING ELSE (d6=5). *** They decline the walk and they decline it sensibly: they are not party to the gnome bargain, were never told the terms, and Dave's own line to Wend on the 96th was that showing them the caves is THE EXTENT OF THE ARRANGEMENT. Walking round the foot of a hill after somebody else's iron is not the caves. *** WHAT THEY ASK FOR INSTEAD IS TO GO BACK IN. *** Which is what Brand came sixty miles north from Draycot's country to do, and what the pair of them failed at for WEEKS before the party walked out of the dark at them -- they never once got past the entrance corridor, and the one time they went in properly they triggered the magic mouths and Orm sat in a corridor for forty minutes rather than admit a wall had frightened him. Now he knows the mouths are noise and nothing, he knows the pair-2 bypass because Dave SHOWED him, and he has heard the whole price list: Torsat to -1, Dellie to 0 off a kobold, two clerics down in three days, Kell dead before the party ever met the road crew. *** IT IS A REQUEST AND NOT A DEMAND, AND THE PARTY OWES THEM NOTHING. What they do not have is a light: the party holds both remaining lanterns and every flask, nine of which are Durnhak's. ***

*** THE PARTY SHOWS TWO STRANGERS ITS MAP OF QUASQUETON LEVEL 1 AND TELLS THEM EVERYTHING, UNASKED, FOR NOTHING -- AND BRAND CANNOT READ IT. *** (d6=2: gratitude and not much retention; they are not map readers.) Eleven expeditions of survey spread on a cloak in the daylight, and the big man is polite and completely lost -- he can follow a finger while it is moving and loses the whole thing the moment it stops. Orm does a little better and not much. *** WHAT THEY CAN ACTUALLY CARRY AWAY IS SPOKEN, AND THAT IS THE THIRD TIME THIS DISTRICT HAS TAUGHT THE PARTY THE SAME LESSON: Sarn could not read and asked to learn, ROWE OFFERS IT AS A DISQUALIFICATION, and now Brand. A written thing is worth nothing to most people here. *** So the briefing that matters is a short spoken list: do not walk the x=16 corridor, use the pair-2 slab, what came out of which door and where two of them nearly died. NOTHING WAS ASKED IN RETURN AND NOTHING WAS OFFERED -- and note that the gifts-land-badly finding does NOT reach this, per articles.md's scope box: these are not dependents, not in Wethersby, hold no debt they cannot pay, and Brand has refused pay twice. *** AND A CALL MADE THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN MADE ON DAY 6: NOBODY HAS EVER SAID WHO DRAWS THIS PARTY'S MAP. *** The cautious MAPPING rate has been charged for twelve expeditions, so somebody has been drawing throughout. It is FRYTHON -- he writes everything else in this party, including the day-55 account to Master Wace in his own hand.

*** THREE RIDE THE LOOP AND FIND THAT THE ROAD ENDS. *** Dave, Yrtone and Hask took the three horses from the watercourse mouth at about half past four while the other six walked the goat-line home; a fighter, a cleric with cures, and a second fighter, which is the right trio to send anywhere alone. THEY DID NOT RIDE DUE WEST -- they cut SOUTH-WEST on the sensible line, 3.7 miles of open rough waste, and d6=4: IT RIDES, CAREFULLY, AND THEY MADE THE ROAD ABOUT SUNSET. Nothing met (d6=2). *** THE FINDING, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THEY WENT FOR: ABOUT A MILE NORTH OF THE CRAG TURNING THE NORTH ROAD SIMPLY STOPS (d6=2). *** The made way frays to a cart-width of beaten dirt and then to grass -- no milestone, no ditch, no maintenance, nothing beyond. Ninety-eight days of calling the crag turning 'the outer limit of the day's-walk patrol circuit' and it is the PARTY'S limit and very nearly the WORLD'S. *** THAT IS ALSO THE ANSWER TO A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED: why a stronghold forty years empty sat unlooted within a day's walk of a market town. Because there is no traffic north of here at all. *** AND ON THE CART QUESTION THE RIDE WAS SENT TO SETTLE: the waste is BETTER GOING PER MILE than the scree and NEARLY TWICE AS FAR -- 3.7 miles against 2 round the north foot -- so d6=4 and not 5-6, and neither route is plainly right for the 101st. Home up Coll's trail in the dark on ground they have walked a dozen times.

*** DAVE OFFERS HASK A CART OF GOODS AND THE TAKINGS. HASK SAYS YES AND ASKS WHICH MULE. *** (d6=2: he says yes and nothing more; d6=2 on what he raises: the practical -- which cart, which mule, who drives.) THE PROPOSAL: Hask carts the salvage south on the 99th and sells at the DAY-100 MARKET while the rest stay for the gnomes on the 101st. *** THREE THINGS MAKE THIS LAND AND THE PLAYER HIT ALL THREE WITHOUT BEING PROMPTED. (1) IT IS WORK AND NOT A GIFT -- articles.md's gifts-fail-work-lands table, the most useful behavioural note in the campaign. (2) HASK ASKED FOR EXACTLY THIS ONCE BEFORE: day 32, 'sell the shears now', and he asked to do the selling himself. (3) DAVE TOOK HIM ASIDE, which honours npcs.md's note in so many words -- HE WILL NOT CHOOSE IN AN AUDIENCE. *** AND THE RESTRAINT IS THE CHARACTERISATION. A man who robbed roads for twenty-two years, who confessed it to Halm's face unprompted, and for whom DAVE PERSONALLY STOOD SURETY with his purse and his name, is handed a cart of goods to sell and the money to carry back -- and he does not make a speech, does not raise his past, does not thank anybody. He asks which cart, which mule, and who drives. *** THE TRUST IS SIMPLY ACCEPTED, WHICH IS A LARGER THING THAN ANY SPEECH WOULD HAVE BEEN. *** He is 41 and he has been offered a job.

*** HASK TAKES DELLIE, ALONE (d6=1), AND HE CANNOT READ OR RECKON (d6=2). *** THE PICK IS THE RECORD'S OWN: Dellie is one of his four off the road, 'sharp, says little, means it', the FIRST of the four to accept giving up the road -- and npcs.md says outright that she DECIDES FOR HASK WHEN HE CAN'T. He is not taking a bodyguard, he is taking his judgment. She is also a cleric now with a cure and two lights she has never used. *** DM CORRECTION, AND THE PROCESS WAS WRONG EVEN THOUGH THE ANSWER CAME OUT RIGHT: the DM asserted last message that Hask 'cannot read or reckon a column' WITH NOTHING IN THE RECORD BEHIND IT. Ninety-eight days and his literacy was never established. Rolled honestly on declared bands afterwards and it came up 1-2 -- neither letters nor figures -- so the claim was TRUE BY LUCK. Being right by accident after asserting without evidence is still the error, and it is the same shape as quoting a running total off a prose file. *** THE CLERK QUESTION IS ANSWERED BETTER THAN IT WAS ASKED. Dave said 'Sarn or Tam' and articles.md art.13 has moved past that: Wend's day-54 line was 'Sarn can count and can't read; Tam can write and can't count -- between the pair of them there's already a clerk in that barn'. *** BUT SARN LEARNED. He wrote the FAIR COPY OF THE STANDING STRUCTURE IN HIS OWN HAND ON DAY 72, four weeks after he could not read his own name, witnessed by Ottir. That was twenty-six days ago. SARN IS NOT HALF A CLERK ANY MORE; HE IS A CLERK, and L025 has him on Coll's standing roll at a clerk's wage for precisely this. *** Hask takes the kettle advice without argument -- he knows he cannot judge it and says so by not pretending otherwise. AND NOTE WHAT THE WHOLE OFFER ANSWERS: npcs.md records Hask going 'flat and directionless once the crisis passed -- you keep handing me the reins and I've got nothing to steer with.' Dave has just handed him a cart, a market and the takings.

*** BRAND'S ACCOUNT OF GOING IN ALONE, AND HE VOLUNTEERS THE ONE THING HE DID NOT HAVE TO. *** They used the pair-2 bypass, which Dave showed them, and got in and out on three torches. NOTHING MUCH CAME OF IT (sealed d6=3, rolled before they set off so it could not be shaped by the evening): no fight, no find, no monster seen. What they mostly proved is that the map they could not read was no use to them and the SPOKEN list was. *** AND THEN, UNASKED, BEFORE ANYBODY HAS BEEN NEAR THE PLACE: THEY FOUND THE PARTY'S CACHE IN THE SMITHY. *** Tristle described that store room to them on day 95 -- the bars, the charcoal, the tools -- so they went and looked at it, and the fire pit had been disturbed enough to notice. They dug the ash off, saw eight torches, thirteen spikes and eight and a half person-weeks of food, TOOK NOTHING, and covered it back over. *** d6=5 on what had been at the ash: SOMETHING WITH HANDS, MOVED AND PUT BACK -- and the answer walked down the hill with them and said so at the fire rather than being found out on the 99th. *** Two men living on a heel of bread and hard cheese between them, alone in a dungeon, standing over eight and a half person-weeks of another man's rations. They put the ash back.

*** DAVE HANDS THE QUESTION BACK -- 'I'd rather you tell me what you want to be' -- AND BRAND HAS NO ANSWER (d6=2). *** The right question, and he is not ready for it. He came sixty miles north from Draycot's country on the party's reputation, failed to get past a corridor for weeks, has refused pay twice, and ASKED TO BE DEFINED BECAUSE BEING TOLD IS EASIER THAN DECIDING. Handed it back, he stands there with it and says so. *** THAT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS WEND'S FLAT 12 ON DAY 54 -- 'you've asked me the right thing and I don't have a clean answer, and that's the problem, not the question' -- and it is the documented double edge of Dave's signature move: asking got 101 on day 41 and 12 on day 54, and the difference was whether the person had an answer waiting. *** AND THEN ORM ANSWERS FOR HIMSELF, WHICH HE HAS NEVER DONE (d6=4): SMALL AND CONCRETE -- HE WOULD TAKE A WAGE. *** Four days of being spoken of as a pair and the two men separate the instant they are asked separately: the loud one cannot say what he wants and the quiet one can, and what he wants is money for work. *** THE RULES ALREADY DRAW THAT LINE AND rules/abilities.md HAS IT CACHED: PHB p.13 -- max henchmen 'does not affect the number of mercenary soldiers, men-at-arms, servitors, and similar persons IN THE PAY of the character', and the campaign's own gloss is 'four ex-bandits taking wages are hirelings, not henchmen'. SO ORM IS ASKING TO BE A HIRELING AND BRAND'S REFUSAL OF PAY IS THE ONE THING THAT WOULD MAKE HIM A HENCHMAN. *** Dave's CHA is 10: FOUR henchmen maximum, loyalty base normal, and -- this party's standing curse -- NO reaction adjustment whatsoever.

*** BOTH ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWERS SPLIT THEM PROPERLY. *** ORM (d6=1): takes it plainly and is content. A wage in town is exactly what he asked for and he is not offended at being kept off the payroll underground -- and the sharp reply that was available to him, that he has ALREADY carried seventy feet of chain up a shaft rope and a 150 lb kettle down the outcrop for nothing, he does not make. He is a straightforward man who asked for a straightforward thing and got it. *** BRAND (d6=3): ASKS FOR THE ADVICE STRAIGHT AWAY. *** Dave's answer -- 'it sounds like you want to learn our trade; you must pick your own profession and I cannot pick it for you, but I will advise' -- is THE DAY-39 MOMENT OFFERED TO A STRANGER, and rules/zero-level.md is the file that governs it: 1e has NO 0-level progression, 1st level BEGINS at 0 XP, and THE GATE IS CAPACITY, NOT POINTS. That is precisely how Hask, Dellie and Ista went from henchmen to Fighter, Cleric and Thief with their scores rolled IN THE OPEN. *** AND HERE IS THE THING NOBODY KNOWS INCLUDING BRAND: FIVE OF HIS SIX SCORES HAVE NEVER BEEN ROLLED. *** Only STRENGTH, forced on day 98 by a kettle -- and it came up NINE, which is the exact minimum a fighter requires and carries no bonus of any kind. The big bare-armed fighting man is, on the one number anybody has, THE WEAKEST LEGAL FIGHTER THERE IS. Dave cannot advise him toward a trade until somebody knows what he has got, and the party has done that before, in the open, for three people, on the 39th.

*** BRAND'S ABILITY SCORES, ROLLED IN THE OPEN, AND THEY EXPLAIN THE MAN. *** DMG p.11 'Special Characters, Including Henchmen' -- 3d6 full range, the identical method Hask, Dellie and Ista got on day 39, with the germane-ability boost held back until a class is fixed so the gate is honest. STR 9 (4,4,1) was already on record off a kettle on the 98th. THE OTHER FIVE: INT 10 (6,1,3) -- WIS 15 (5,6,4) -- DEX 11 (4,5,2) -- CON 12 (1,6,5) -- CHA 4 (2,1,1). *** THE BIG BARE-ARMED FIGHTING MAN WITH THE HAND AXE HAS WISDOM AS HIS BEST SCORE BY THREE CLEAR POINTS, AND A CHARISMA OF FOUR. *** Nobody at the table would have guessed either. *** AND CHA 4 IS THE ANSWER TO THE WHOLE OF LAST NIGHT: max 1 henchman, loyalty base -25%, REACTION ADJUSTMENT -20% (PHB p.13, rules/abilities.md). He asked Dave to tell him what he was, and said outright that being told is easier -- because a man with a 4 cannot carry a room and has never once been able to. It was not modesty. It was an accurate self-assessment. *** LEGAL CLASSES: Fighter (STR 9, exactly), Cleric (WIS 9), Thief (DEX 9), Magic-User (INT 9) -- all four basics. Paladin, Ranger, Druid, Monk and Assassin ALL FAIL, three of them on the Charisma alone.

*** THE FOUR TRADES EXPLAINED, THE WISDOM POINTED AT -- AND BRAND PUSHES BACK (d6=5), AND IN PUSHING BACK SAYS THE THING NOBODY HAS HEARD. *** TWO REFUSALS, both consistent with every other thing he has done. (1) HE HAS NO FAITH AT ALL (d6=1) AND HAS NEVER BEEN INSIDE A CHAPEL. He will not take a god he does not have any more than he will take money he has not earned -- and the party of all people should recognise the shape of that, because it is the same refusal they have watched him make twice. *** NOTE WHAT THIS EXPOSES: NINETY-NINE DAYS AND THIS CAMPAIGN HAS NEVER NAMED A DEITY. It has chapels, almoners, a HOUSE that Cuddy writes to and a superior above him. Yrtone and Blartho BEGAN as clerics and nobody ever asked them what they serve. Brand would be CONVERTING AT FORTY-ONE, which is a different act, and somebody would have to RECEIVE him -- and the obvious man is FATHER CUDDY, a 3rd-level cleric fifty-seven miles south-west who is already owed a letter. *** (2) AND THE THING NOBODY HAS HEARD: HE KNOWS HE IS NOT STRONG. *** He has been big-framed since he was a boy, men have assumed, and he has let them -- and STR 9 is the coldest confirmation possible, the exact minimum a fighter requires with no bonus of any kind. What has kept him alive for forty-one years is not his arms. IT IS KNOWING WHEN TO STOP. *** WHICH REWRITES THE ELEVEN FAILURES AT THAT CORRIDOR. He did not fail eleven times; HE TURNED BACK ELEVEN TIMES, out of a place that has put this party on the floor four times and killed a man before they ever met the road crew. That is not cowardice and it is not incapacity. IT IS THE ONLY SANE ASSESSMENT ANYBODY HAS EVER MADE OF QUASQUETON, and it is what a WISDOM OF 15 ON A SHEET OF 9s AND 10s AND A 4 actually looks like from the inside. *** The class question is wide open and he has earned the right to have it stay open.

*** NARRATION CORRECTION, PLAYER-CAUGHT: 'The characters aren't looking at a sheet with his numbers on it.' *** The DM wrote Dave POINTING AT THE SHEET and saying the wisdom was the thing, and Brand TAPPING THE 9 ON IT with one enormous finger. Neither can happen. *** ABILITY SCORES ARE ROLLED IN THE OPEN FOR THE PLAYER -- that is a fairness commitment, it makes the gate honest and stops the DM shaping an NPC's capacity to suit the evening -- BUT THERE IS NO SHEET INSIDE THE FICTION AND NOBODY IN IT CAN SEE A NUMBER. *** The substance of the scene all stands and none of it needed a sheet: the party explained four trades and said he has a better head on him than he lets on, WHICH THEY KNOW FROM FOUR DAYS OF WATCHING HIM. He refused on two grounds he stated in his own words -- no faith and never inside a chapel, and he has always known he is not strong and has let men assume otherwise since he was twelve. A man can say all of that about himself without reading a number, and it is stronger for being testimony rather than arithmetic. *** THE OBSERVATIONS THE PARTY ACTUALLY HAS: he turned back eleven times and was right every time; he could not read their map and said so; he carried the light end of the kettle; nobody follows him and he asked to be TOLD what he was. That is the evidence in the room, and it points the same way the dice do WITHOUT anybody quoting them. *** This is the mirror of CHECKLIST section 8 -- that governs what the PLAYER may not be told; this governs what the CHARACTERS cannot know.

*** SECOND NARRATION CORRECTION IN A ROW, AND THIS ONE IS A REASONING ERROR NOT A STAGING ONE. PLAYER: 'Why does he say we have the wrong idea of him? If we had the wrong idea of him we would have suggested fighter.' *** DEAD RIGHT. The DM gave Brand the line 'you've the wrong idea of me anyway' -- A REBUTTAL TO AN ARGUMENT NOBODY MADE. The party had just told him the opposite of the wrong idea: that his HEAD is the part worth training and not his arms. That is the RIGHT idea of him, arrived at independently off four days of watching, and I had him argue against it. *** THE CAUSE IS A STORY-SHAPED REFLEX: 'character reveals hidden truth' got pattern-matched onto 'character corrects a misapprehension', when the scene had already skipped that step. The party got there FIRST. *** THE CORRECTED BEAT IS BETTER AND THE d6=5 STILL HOLDS: he pushes back ON THE CLERIC ONLY, on the ground that he has no faith and has never been inside a chapel, AND HE AGREES WITH THE DIAGNOSIS WHILE REFUSING THE PRESCRIPTION. What nobody has heard comes out as CONFIRMATION, not rebuttal: he has known since he was twelve that he is not strong, he has let men assume it for twenty-nine years because it got him fed, and SEVEN STRANGERS WHO HAVE KNOWN HIM FOUR DAYS ARE THE FIRST PEOPLE EVER TO SEE IT. *** That is a far heavier thing to put on a man than an argument, and it costs the scene nothing to be true.

*** TRISTLE AND FRYTHON GIVE THE LAST TWO TRADES STRAIGHT, AND BRAND NAMES THE ANSWER NOBODY OFFERED HIM (d6=5): TEACH ME TO READ. *** NOT A CLASS. THE PREREQUISITE. *** THE HONEST FIGURES, which is what made it a real choice rather than a menu: as a 1st-level HUMAN thief at boosted DEX 14 every Dexterity adjustment on PHB p.12 Table II is ZERO and he gets no racial bonus, so he would have the bare PHB p.28 line -- Hide in Shadows 10%, Move Silently 15%, Hear Noise 10%, Find/Remove Traps 20%, Open Locks 25%. TRISTLE, elf at DEX 18, runs 30/30/15/25/35. *** BRAND WOULD BE WORSE THAN THE THIEF THEY ALREADY HAVE AT EVERY SINGLE THING, and Tristle told him so, because Tristle's own record is a catalogue of failed percentages -- two blown Find/Remove Traps on the area 36 pit and the skill spent until 2nd level. AND FRYTHON'S TRADE BEGINS WITH READING, which Brand cannot do. *** SO HE DECLINED TO CHOOSE, AND THAT IS THE MOST IN-CHARACTER THING HE COULD POSSIBLY HAVE DONE. A man whose one gift is knowing when to put the axe down, told an hour ago that his judgment is the part worth training, applied it to the decision in front of him: refused to commit on insufficient information and asked for the thing that opens every door instead of the thing that shuts three. *** AND IT COSTS HIM NOTHING, WHICH THE PARTY MAY NOT REALISE: rules/zero-level.md, 1st level BEGINS at 0 XP and the gate is CAPACITY not points, so there is no clock and no penalty for deciding later. A 5e-shaped intuition would make delay expensive. 1e does not. *** THE PRECEDENT IS FOUR WEEKS OLD AND IT IS FRYTHON'S: Sarn could not read his own name on day 39 and wrote the fair copy of the standing structure in his own hand on day 72. Frython is now the party's teacher twice over, and the second pupil is a berserker of forty-one.

*** FIRST CONTACT WITH ORCS THAT IS NOT A FIGHT, AFTER NINETY-NINE DAYS OF KILLING THEM. *** The whole party in ONE square at (2,24) -- player correction, and it is right: party.tsv has always tracked a single coordinate and the DM had invented a three-square column out of the rank list. They STOP AND WAIT. Dave swaps sword-and-shield for the short bow, which rules/combat.md prices at THE WHOLE ROUND and which is free here because nothing can reach them without coming round two corners; it costs him a point of AC while the shield is slung and nothing else. *** TRISTLE ANSWERS IN ORCISH: 'Yes we have killed many of them. Who asks?' *** Straight, truthful, no threat, and a question back -- the identical move that got 75 out of Durnhak and 100 out of Brand. And for orcs specifically, admitting to killing many lizard-men IS NOT A CONFESSION, IT IS A CREDENTIAL. *** REACTION 33 on DMG p.63: UNCERTAIN, 55% prone toward NEGATIVE -- and the lean rolled 99, which tips it the other way by four points off the far end of a forty-five-point band. *** Then d6=6: HE GIVES MORE THAN HE NEEDED TO. A name -- RUK -- and the reason he asked, which is that the lizard-men killed three of his. He has not moved, his weapons are out, and thirty feet of corridor is still thirty feet. UNCERTAIN IS NOT FRIENDLY. *** THE CHANNEL IS THE SAME ONE AS THE GNOMES: party_roster.md line 75, the elf racial language list, used for the second time in four days after ninety-five days of never being used at all.

*** CORRECTION: 'THE FIRST ORC IN NINETY-NINE DAYS NOT KILLED ON SIGHT' IS FALSE, AND IT IS FALSE TWICE. *** (1) PLAYER, out of game: an orc was encountered on level 1 AND SCARED AWAY. That event is in NO LOG -- not world_changes, not encounters, not the DM notes, not the archived sessions. It is narrated-but-never-recorded, which is this campaign's oldest and most documented failure mode and the entire reason the TSVs exist. THE PLAYER'S MEMORY IS THE ONLY COPY. *** (2) AND THE SHARPER ONE IS ALREADY ON THE RECORD WHERE I COULD HAVE READ IT. B1_DM_NOTES, expedition 4, turn 14, three orcs out of the second-pair doors: 'FRYTHON SHOUTED IN COMMON; ROLLED 20% FOR COMPREHENSION, FAILED. NO PARLEY.' *** SO THE PARTY TRIED TO TALK TO ORCS FIFTY-THREE DAYS AGO AND FAILED ON LANGUAGE ALONE -- and TRISTLE WAS ON THAT EXPEDITION AND HAS SPOKEN ORCISH SINCE CHARACTER GENERATION. *** The channel existed at turn 14 of expedition 4 and nobody remembered it, which is the IDENTICAL failure as the gnome line going unused for ninety-five days until day 95. Twice now, the same sheet, the same forgotten row. *** WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE about today: it is the first orc contact this party has managed to CONDUCT -- to ask and be answered -- and that is a claim about the language and not about the party's intentions, which were peaceable on expedition 4 and simply could not be transmitted.

*** NO FIGHT. RUK YIELDS THE CORRIDOR (d6=3) -- grudgingly, westward, and he watches them go past. *** Tristle's line refused the demand without threatening it: 'We'll let you go by, but we go where we go.' It CONCEDES SOMETHING REAL -- the party will not attack, and eight of them against four in a 10-ft corridor with a sleep spell in reserve very much could -- AND YIELDS NOTHING. Same register as every exchange this party has ever won: honest, no threat, no submission. *** AND RUK HAD A CLEAN WAY OUT THE WHOLE TIME that the party could not see: west from (4,19) to (3,19) to (2,19), then SOUTH TO (2,18), ground nobody in this party has ever laid eyes on. He never needed to pass them. He wanted them to turn round, and when they would not, the ground was worth less to him than four orcs. *** FIRST TIME IN A HUNDRED DAYS THAT THIS PARTY AND A GROUP OF ORCS HAVE BEEN IN A CORRIDOR TOGETHER AND NOBODY DIED -- on expedition 4 the party tried to talk and failed on language, and on 4, 5 and 6 every orc met was killed. The difference today is one line on one character sheet. *** WHAT IT COSTS THEM: the orcs now know where the party is going, they are WEST AND BEHIND once the party turns into the smithy, and the party has NO IRON SPIKES to seal a door with -- the thirteen it owns are under the ash it is walking to. The moment they dig up the cache that changes.

*** HOW THE POLE ERROR SURVIVED A CORRECTION, DIAGNOSED BY THE PLAYER -- AND IT IS A FAILURE MODE OF THE CORRECTION LOOP ITSELF, NOT OF EITHER PARTY. *** Player, day 99: 'you said we had left the poles on the cart, and I said we wouldn't leave them on the cart (which is true) but I made the wrong correction, since that was irrelevant and they were in the smithy.' *** THE MECHANISM: the DM asserted a FALSE PREMISE (poles in the cart at the basecamp). The player rejected it on TRUE grounds (tools are not freight and never were). The DM checked the premise against inventory_log, found holder 'spread', and both parties came away satisfied -- WITH THE ACTUAL FACT STILL WRONG, because it lived in a THIRD file: world_changes' day-95 area-state text, 'three ten-foot poles left in a corner, not hidden'. *** A REBUTTAL ONLY TESTS THE PREMISE IT WAS AIMED AT. A false premise can therefore draw a correct objection to a question nobody needed answered, and the agreement that follows feels like verification and is not. *** WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: the party was two days from standing in that room, and world.py deployed / the area-state text on area 18 would have said so. THE LESSON IS NARROW AND USEFUL -- when the DM is corrected about WHERE A THING IS, check every log that can hold a location, not the one that raised the claim. inventory_log has now been the wrong one three times this week: the phantom lantern, the double-counted spikes, and the poles.

*** BACKFILL, LOGGED ON DAY 99 BECAUSE log.py REFUSED A DAY-99 SCENE THAT NAMED HIM: 'no person durnhak in campaign/people.tsv'. *** He has been the most consequential NPC in this campaign for four days -- 588 lb of iron, half of everything it makes, a back door into the crag, a standing trade in rope and spikes and oil, and an L053 that has been noted five times -- AND HE WAS NEVER IN THE PEOPLE REFERENCE, so entities.py who Durnhak returned 'no person Durnhak' and scene 95:1 named only Tristle and Dave. THE GNOME WAS NOT A PARTICIPANT IN HIS OWN NEGOTIATION. *** WHY IT HAPPENED: loops.tsv's subject column is FREE TEXT and takes 'durnhak' without complaint, so L053 read perfectly for four days while the join table had no idea he existed. A reference file is only enforced where something validates against it. *** This row exists so his day-95 scene has him in it. The terms are on people.tsv and in L053; nothing here is new.

*** THE FIRST TIME EITHER OF THEM HAS SEEN THE OTHER'S FACE. *** 'You must be Durnhak, I presume' is a man identifying A VOICE -- because the whole of the day-95 bargain was struck THROUGH A THREE-FOOT SHAFT, forty feet of it, with a lantern lowered on a rope. Half of what this party owns underground was negotiated by two people who had never laid eyes on each other. *** HE IS BUSINESSLIKE AND A LITTLE CAUGHT-OUT (d6=2). He confirms it. He reports the work: 588 LB OFF THE CRAG IN FOUR DAYS, the exact figure he counted on his fingers on the 95th. AND HE DOES NOT PRETEND HE CAME UP A FORTY-FOOT SHAFT FOR THE VIEW -- he was checking whether more bar had been dropped and he says so, which is the same instinct as refusing the pay-up-front and telling them where his own back door is. *** HE DOES NOT ASK FOR MONEY. The terms say a quarter at the hole WHEN THE BARS ARE COUNTED; they are counted; about 37 gp is due. THE PARTY IS CARRYING IT, under the standing rule the player set today -- coin is either with Wend or on their persons and there is no third place. A caught-out man does not open with a demand. He reports and waits. *** AND HIS POSITION IS BAD AND HE KNOWS IT: two gnomes at a shaft head in a room with one LOCKED door and one that has just swung open on eight armed humans and a lamp. NOBODY DREW ON HIM. That is twice in ten minutes this party has declined to start something it would have won.

*** TRISTLE WAVES THE WHOLE THING OFF -- 'that's your right, we don't own this place' -- GIVES HIM THE ORC INTELLIGENCE FOR NOTHING, AND OFFERS HIM A CHOICE INSTEAD OF PRESSING HIM. And Durnhak asks the thing nobody expected (d6=5). *** HE DOES NOT ASK ABOUT THE MONEY OR THE GOODS. He asks whether the orcs have been in THIS ROOM. *** AND THE REASON IS SITTING IN THE MIDDLE OF THE FLOOR AND THE PARTY HAS NEVER ONCE SEEN IT THAT WAY ROUND. TO THE PARTY THE SHAFT IS A CHUTE -- four days ago they dropped 28 iron bars down it and lowered a lit lantern on a rope. TO DURNHAK IT IS HIS CEILING. *** A three-foot hole, forty feet, opening directly into the workings where five gnomes sleep. Anything that gets into area 19 does not need to find a way down; the way down is already cut, and it was cut by somebody else. The party has been treating a two-way door as a one-way delivery. *** He wants to know what has been in this room, and he wants to know whether the thing that has been killing the lizard-men now knows where his front hall is. NOBODY HAS TOLD HIM ABOUT THE FOUR ORCS' GRIEVANCE, only that they exist. *** AND THERE IS AN IRON RING BOLTED TO THE WALL BESIDE THE SHAFT, logged on day 95 and never explained, which means somebody once had a reason to fasten something over or above that hole.

*** TRISTLE GIVES HIM THE ANSWER FOR NOTHING AND DURNHAK SPOTS THE JOKE IN IT HIMSELF (d6=5). *** The advice: spike both doors of area 19 FROM INSIDE and the room becomes a lid. It works precisely because his people do not use the doors -- THEY COME UP THE HOLE -- so sealing the room from within costs them nothing and shuts everything else out. The party has been in and out of that room twice and never once thought of it as a lid. *** AND THEN HE WORKS OUT WHAT HE ORDERED. On the 95th, out of his own seventy-five, he asked for six coils of rope, twenty pounds of timber nails, a dozen flasks of oil AND TWO HUNDRED IRON SPIKES -- for rope-work and hauling, four days of slinging bar up a watercourse. *** THE SPIKES ARE THE EXACT TOOL FOR A PROBLEM HE DISCOVERED NINETY SECONDS AGO, AND THEY ARE ALREADY BOUGHT, ALREADY PAID FOR OUT OF HIS OWN SHARE, AND SITTING IN A CART AT THE BASECAMP. *** He did not need the party to point it out and they did not get the chance. *** NOTHING WAS ASKED FOR AND NOTHING WAS GIVEN: the party is carrying thirteen spikes and he did not ask for one of them, which is consistent with a man who would rather owe less than be handed anything. The 101st now has a second reason to happen.

*** BOTH THIEVES FAIL AND THE GNOME OFFERS THE ANSWER UNASKED (d6=3). *** Not about the lock -- he is a scavenger who strips old workings, not a lockpick, and gnomes have no such ability. His trade is taking apart things that do not want taking apart, so his opinion is about HINGES. *** AND THE HINGES ARE ON THIS SIDE. *** The door opens TOWARD area 19 (d6=6, day 95), and this campaign cached the consequence on day 81 at (30,37,V): 'POSSIBLE ONLY BECAUSE IT OPENS TOWARD THE PARTY -- the hinges are on this face.' Ten feet south at (30,33,V) they were on the far side and there was nothing to oil. THE SAME GEOMETRY THAT DECIDES WHICH SPIKE METHOD WORKS DECIDES THIS. *** CUT THE HINGES, NOT THE LOCK. *** B1 p.7: doors are 'uniformly of heavy wooden construction, approximately five or six inches thick' -- but hinge PINS are iron, and the party owns FOUR HACKSAWS whose own inventory row says why they were taken: 'A hacksaw cuts METAL, which is the point of taking it -- this party has spiked, prised and levered its way through four expeditions and has never once had a way to cut iron.' *** THE COST IS KNOWN AND IT IS NOT FREE: day 98, four turns of hacksaw on two ceiling bolts rolled d6=1 on the noise band and bought the first clock.py extra in the campaign's history. Sawing hinges will be a roll, not a certainty -- which is better than breaking the door down, where B1's front matter makes the extra check automatic. *** DURNHAK IS NOT OFFERING TO DO IT. He points, says the thing, and leaves it with them.

*** THE PARTING, AND IT IS THE WARMEST THING EITHER SIDE HAS SAID. 'Glad we ran into you, take care and we'll see you in two days.' *** Two days is DAY 101 at the mouth of the dry watercourse, which the party has now WALKED TO -- they found it on the 98th off his spoken bearing and it was exact. *** WHAT CHANGED IN TWELVE MINUTES OF STANDING IN A CHARCOAL STORE: they have seen each other's faces for the first time, having negotiated 588 lb of iron through a three-foot hole; the haul is DONE, four days as he said; he has four spikes in his hands as early delivery and a reason to use them he did not have this morning; the party has the answer to a locked door banked for a day when it is not pressed; and NOBODY ASKED ANYBODY FOR MONEY, though about 37 gp was in the room and the terms said a quarter was due. *** THE ACCOUNT NOW SETTLES IN ONE TRANSACTION ON THE 101st, cash against goods, where both are in the same place -- which is the player's reading and the correct one. *** And the last thing the party does before it goes is spike a door it is not using, to help a man it met on Tuesday keep his ceiling shut.

*** CORRECTION, PLAYER-CAUGHT: RUK WAS NEVER TOLD THE PARTY WAS COMING TO LOOK FOR ORCS. *** The DM wrote that he 'had fifteen turns to be somewhere else after being told to his face that the party was coming to look for orcs, and he used them' -- which puts a sentence in Tristle's mouth that was said to somebody else entirely. *** WHAT WAS ACTUALLY SAID TO RUK, all of it: 'Yes we have killed many of them. Who asks?'; 'I'm Tristle. Although we've killed many of them, they've wounded us many times. Where are the ones that killed your three?'; and, to the demand that they turn round, 'WE'LL LET YOU GO BY, BUT WE GO WHERE WE GO.' Three lines about LIZARD-MEN and one refusal of a demand. Nothing about hunting orcs. *** THE 'find those orcs' LINE WAS SAID TO DURNHAK, twenty minutes later and through a different language, and even there it was a WARNING about what was loose in the hill rather than a declaration of intent. *** WHY IT MATTERS AND IS NOT PEDANTRY: it changes what Ruk knows. On the DM's version he withdrew from a stated hunt. On the record he withdrew from eight armed strangers who would not be turned round and who had told him nothing about their intentions -- which is a colder and more ordinary thing, and leaves entirely open whether he is watching, gone, or waiting. *** CHECKLIST section 8b: the DM does not put words in the party's mouth, and the tell is always that the invented line sounded good.

*** 'ARE YOU RUK'S?' -- AND THE NAME MEANS NOTHING TO THEM (d6=1). *** Which is the discovery, and it came out of one question in a language nobody else in this party speaks. THE ORCS IN THIS HILL ARE NOT ONE COMMUNITY. Two pairs of them within a hundred feet and one has never heard the other's name. Everything the party has assumed about 'the orcs' as a single faction -- on expeditions 4, 5 and 6, and in Tristle's price-list to Brand -- was an assumption. *** REACTION 71 on DMG p.63: uncertain, 55% prone toward POSITIVE, and the lean rolled 36, which tips it the good way. Tristle CHA 9, no adjustment, as this party has never had one. *** AND THEY GIVE GROUND WITHOUT ANSWERING (d6=5). Two orcs come round a corner into a lamp and eight armed people, get asked an incomprehensible question about somebody they have never heard of, and BACK AWAY DOWN THE PIPE. No fight, no answer, no bargain. *** THE SECOND ORC GROUP IN ONE EXPEDITION TO WITHDRAW RATHER THAN CHARGE, AND THE THIRD ENCOUNTER TODAY TO END WITHOUT A BLOW -- Ruk's four, these two, and Durnhak's pair at the shaft. *** AND WHAT THE MAP MAKES CERTAIN: with no branches in that corridor, THEY ARE BACKING DOWN IT TOWARD RUK'S FOUR. Two groups who do not know each other are about to be in the same ten-foot channel, and the party will not see what happens.

*** THE SAME OFFER RUK GOT, WITH THE GEOMETRY REVERSED -- AND IT IS A FAR BIGGER ASK THIS TIME. *** 'You head north. You go by us, we let you leave. Then we continue.' With Ruk it cost him nothing: he had a clean line of retreat and never needed to pass anybody. THESE TWO ARE BEING ASKED TO WALK SINGLE FILE PAST EIGHT ARMED PEOPLE IN A TEN-FOOT CORRIDOR, inside the reach of a sword and under two bows and three loaded slings. The party is offering its word and asking for their bodies. *** THEY WILL NOT DO IT (d6=4), AND THEY ARE RIGHT NOT TO. No reasonable creature accepts that trade from strangers who have admitted killing many of something. *** BUT THEY GIVE UP THE TURN. *** They back round the corner and are gone out of the light -- which hands the party the one thing it actually wanted, because the corner was never the prize, the KNOWLEDGE OF WHICH WAY IT GOES was. *** FOURTH ENCOUNTER TODAY TO END WITHOUT A BLOW, and the third time an orc has chosen to give ground rather than fight. Ruk's four, Durnhak's pair, these two twice over. The party has met ten creatures in this hill today and not swung at one of them. *** No second reaction roll: the 71 stands. Re-rolling p.63 through a conversation is the error this campaign named on 2026-08-30.

*** THE PARTY HAD TWO FREE SURPRISE SEGMENTS, THREE BOWS AND TWO LOADED SLINGS AT THIRTY FEET, AND SPENT THEM SAYING HELLO. *** Tristle laughs first -- which is the detail that makes it land -- then, in orcish: 'Hello again. We're going west. Watch out for the troglodytes.' A greeting, a declaration of intent, and A FREE GIFT OF THE ONE PIECE OF INTELLIGENCE THE PARTY HAS, handed to two orcs who do not know Ruk and therefore do not know what the lizard-men did to his. *** NO NEW REACTION ROLL. The 71 stands; re-rolling p.63 through a conversation is the error named on 2026-08-30. This was a d6 on what they DO, and it came up 5: THEY ANSWER AND GIVE SOMETHING BACK. *** AND WHAT THEY GIVE IS A WARNING ABOUT THE WEST -- the direction the party has just announced. In his words and not in anybody's bestiary: DEAD THINGS, WEST. THEY TAKE HOLD OF YOU AND THEN YOU CANNOT MOVE. *** No name, no count, no description beyond that. He has no word for what it is and no interest in one; what he has is what it does to people he knew. *** THAT CLAUSE IS WORTH MORE TO THIS PARTY THAN THE IRON IT IS CARRYING. Hit points run 2 to 9 across eight people and three of them are on 2 or 3. Something that holds you still in a ten-foot corridor does not need to be strong. *** FIFTH EXCHANGE TODAY TO END WITHOUT A BLOW, and the fourth time a creature in this hill has given the party something for nothing after being given something for nothing.

*** THE PARTY TURNS ROUND ON AN ORC'S WORD. *** Tristle relays it, the column stops, and after a short conference THEY DO NOT GO WEST. An hour ago they were being told to turn round by Ruk and refused on principle -- 'we go where we go'. Tonight a different orc says 'dead things west, they take hold of you and then you cannot move' AND THEY TAKE IT, immediately, and change a declared plan. *** THE DIFFERENCE IS NOT COURAGE, IT IS INFORMATION: Ruk offered a demand and these two offered a reason, and this party has never once ignored a reason. *** AND TRISTLE'S PARTING LINE LANDS ALL THREE WAYS (d6=5), WITH THE LAST ONE HARDEST: 'Respect the dead. Kill them first or stay away. We'll stay away.' The tactics register -- do not let a thing that holds you get its hands on you. The commitment registers, and to somebody who lives on this road a stranger's promise about where he will not go is worth more than a gift. *** BUT IT IS THE FIRST THREE WORDS THAT STOP HIM, and the reason is not hard: whatever is west was somebody's dead once, and two orcs who have lost people on this road have thought about that for longer than the party has. *** NO WITHDRAWAL SPLIT AFTER ALL -- player corrected the DM's reading: the three with bows COVER while the column passes and then back away WITH it, so the lamp never leaves the party and the light problem the DM raised does not exist. Eight people, one lamp, moving together.

*** CONTACT AT THIRTY FEET, AND THE FIRST HOSTILE REACTION OF THE DAY. 17 on DMG p.63: the 06-25 band, HOSTILE, IMMEDIATE ACTION. *** Five encounters today ended without a blow -- Ruk's four, Durnhak's pair, two orcs twice over -- and every one of them was a roll that could have gone the other way. This one went the other way. *** ONE CREATURE, standing at the edge of Ista's lamplight where the cut stone gives out, seven feet of it. It held deliberately while a lantern came forty feet up a corridor at it, which is not the behaviour of something frightened. *** AND TRISTLE KNOWS WHAT IT IS, BECAUSE HE SPEAKS ITS LANGUAGE. party_roster.md line 75: common, elvish, GNOLL, hobgoblin, gnome, halfling, orcish. *** THAT IS THE THIRD ENTRY ON ONE LINE OF ONE CHARACTER SHEET TO DECIDE AN ENCOUNTER IN FIVE DAYS -- gnome bought 588 lb of iron and a gnome's back door on the 95th; orcish bought two parleys and a warning about the dead this afternoon; and now gnoll, on a thing that has already decided to fight. *** THE SURPRISE ROLL FOR IT WAS VOIDED BEFORE THIS: it had been awake and watching for four rounds and cannot be caught unaware by an arrival it chose to wait for. That cost the party a free volley from three bows and two slings, and it was the right call. NOBODY IS SURPRISED. *** Dave is on the SHORT BOW at AC 4, which is the missile-forward trade rules/combat.md warns about, and at thirty feet it is the right end of it -- for exactly as long as thirty feet lasts.

*** THE SQUARE AT FULL DARK, LOOKING FOR TOLLER, AND THEY DO NOT GET HIM. *** The sealed d6=2 on the shop STANDS and was not re-rolled -- letting a second roll overturn the first because the player pushed is the softening this campaign forbids. But the initiative was not wasted: d6=3 buys a NEIGHBOUR WHO KNOWS WHERE HE SLEEPS AND WHEN HE WILL BE ON THE PITCH. *** THE NEIGHBOUR IS BIRCHER, and the campaign already had him -- the man who offered Halm 9 gp for his cart on day 4 and did not get it, because the party bought Halm a mule instead. He has a pitch two along from Toller's chalk.
