No grudge in it, but he knows exactly who these two are and whose cart he did not buy. *** WHAT HE GIVES THEM, plainly and for nothing: Toller beds at his sister's out the Marchford road, twenty minutes' walk, and carts his stock in to be ON THE PITCH BEFORE FIRST LIGHT. *** d6=1: HASK AND DELLIE ARE NOT FOUND -- both in town for tomorrow's market and logged away for exactly that, but the town is full and dark and they are elsewhere in it. *** THE DECISION IS THE PLAYER'S AND IT HAS A REAL COST: knocking a one-man dealer out of his sister's bed at full dark on the eve of his busiest day is a declared act, and Toller's warmth for tomorrow is ALREADY SEALED AT 4 -- waking him would modify it, and should.

column7: 4 (warmth), 2 (what the books fetch), 3 (scrolls yes / wire no), 4 (the set: an enquiry, no offer)
column8: *** TOLLER ON HIS PITCH BEFORE FIRST LIGHT, EXACTLY WHERE BIRCHER SAID. Warm (d6=4). *** ALL FOUR DETERMINATIONS WERE SEALED ON THE 99th, before the party rode in, so nothing about the evening shaped them. *** (1) THE BOOKS: he goes through all ten properly, which takes a while, and then gives the number without dressing it -- TWENTY-SIX GOLD for the lot. Seven smaller volumes at 2 gp, three large metal-bound at 4 gp because the binding alone is worth something. *** THAT IS A POOR RETURN ON 130 LB HAULED TWENTY-TWO MILES AND IT IS NOT BEING INFLATED. No 1e core book prices a book, so the figure is a DM call on bands declared before the roll, the same procedure as the day-97 timber nails, and the roll came up at the thin end. His reason is the same one he gave them on day 16 when he advised against a city sale: the market here for ordinary books is thin, and ten histories and treatises are stock that SITS. *** THE HONEST CONTRAST, and it is his own valuation not a new one: ZELLIGAR'S DIARY ALONE IS WORTH MORE THAN ALL TEN PUT TOGETHER, because that is a named wizard's hand. *** (2) THE THREE SCROLLS he takes -- squarely his line -- at 1 gp 5 sp the three. (3) THE COPPER WIRE IS NOT HIS BUSINESS and he says so bluntly: that is a smith's, and he names MUND, whom the party already deals with and who bought their at-cost iron in quantity on the 97th. *** (4) THE SET -- the diary, Rogahn's silver plaque and the bed headboard, held on OPEN TERMS since day 32 at reaction 95 with full discretion: AN ENQUIRY AND NO OFFER (d6=4). He volunteers it unasked, which is his record. *** NO SALE IS LOGGED. The offer stands and the decision is the player's; xp on the books and scrolls falls due only if and when they sell (DMG p.85, treasure GAINED -- the bronze-wrestlers precedent).

*** FRYTHON BEGINS TEACHING BRAND HIS LETTERS AT COLL'S BASECAMP, while the party waits on Dave and Tristle. RETCONNED IN AT THE PLAYER'S REQUEST, day 100, and it contradicts nothing: both men were logged at the basecamp all day and L054 already records that BRAND ASKED TO BE TAUGHT TO READ RATHER THAN PICK A CLASS. The only thing added is that the teaching actually started. *** d6=4: SLOW AND STUBBORN, which is the better half of slow. INT 10 is dead average -- no help and no hindrance. He does not give up and he does not pretend to have it. *** WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: Brand is FORTY-ONE, CHA 4, and a man who said outright that being told is easier than deciding. Sitting down in front of a twenty-nine-year-old magic-user to be taught what children are taught is the least comfortable thing he has done, and he asked for it himself. *** AND FRYTHON IS THE RIGHT TEACHER AND THE WORST ONE: INT 17, the only literate-by-trade man in the party, and the one who sat down to the 86-marks arithmetic after 54 days and FAILED it. He knows what it is to be out of his depth in front of a page. *** NOT A CLASS DECISION. L054 stays open: he still has not picked, and letters were always the prerequisite and never the answer.

column7: 5 (there, bars out, and more), 1 (more gnomes), 2d4=5 (ten in all), 4 (warm, remarks on the horses)
column8: *** THE WATERCOURSE, TEN IN THE MORNING, AND TRISTLE GREETS HIM IN GNOME FOR THE SECOND TIME. Warm (d6=4). *** THE BARS ARE OUT AND COUNTED: TWENTY-EIGHT, which is every one the party dropped down the area 19 shaft. The 29th was carried out the front door on day 95 and was never his. *** COUNTING THE BARS IS THE TRIGGER -- his own term, set down the shaft on the 95th. *** HIS RECKONING, stated plainly and in full, which is the whole difference from the day-99 version the DM quoted partially: stores 32 gp 4 sp -- 6 coils of rope, 11 flasks of the 12 asked, the hooded lantern, 200 spikes, 20 lb of nails -- taken off the SEVENTY-FIVE that is his half of what the iron should make. BALANCE 42 gp 6 sp. A QUARTER NOW, 10 gp 7 sp. THIRTY-TWO GOLD WHEN THE IRON SELLS. *** AND THE SEVENTY-FIVE IS AN ESTIMATE AND HE SAYS SO -- the iron has not been sold and his terms were built around exactly that, which is why he refused payment up front: he would rather not be paid for iron that turns out worthless. *** HE IS ONE FLASK SHORT and knows it; Wethersby had two to sell and that was every flask in the town. *** TEN GNOMES ARE VISIBLE, not five. The party has reasoned off 'Durnhak and four others' since day 95, and five is also B1's own maximum for area 38 -- so the number they have been using was the module's and they never knew it. HE DOES NOT EXPLAIN IT AND IS NOT ASKED. NOT VOLUNTEERED, and the arithmetic is theirs to do. *** NO MONEY HAS MOVED. The reckoning is on the table and the figure is not the one the party rode in expecting.

column7: 4 (a real two-way channel), 3 (pleased, and shows it)
column8: *** TRISTLE ASKS FOR A STANDING CHANNEL, NOT A NEXT MEETING -- goods to buy in town, goods to sell in town, or news about the caves. *** THE HARD PART IS HIS OWN CONSTRAINT: 'we cannot go where you go', 'people ask a gnome different questions'. Any arrangement has to work for a partner who cannot walk into a market town. *** d6=4, A REAL TWO-WAY CHANNEL, not a drop-box. HIS PROPOSAL: (1) THE SLAB under the overhang at the watercourse -- word goes beneath it, wrapped against the wet, by either side. (2) A CUT MARK ON THE ROCK AT THE MOUTH, visible from below, meaning there is something under the slab -- so nobody makes the climb for nothing and nobody has to guess. He cuts the mark for them then and there and has Tristle cut it back, twice, until it is right. *** (3) AND THE HALF HE CANNOT SOLVE ALONE: when the party is not at the crag at all -- and it is not, most of the time -- he needs a NAME AT THE BASECAMP. Somebody he can hand a thing to at night and know it reaches Tristle. He will not simply walk up to a camp of humans and trust whoever is awake. *** d6=3: HE IS PLEASED AND SHOWS IT. A man who set his own payment terms to avoid being over-advanced, told them where his back door is, and came up a forty-foot shaft to check on them, is being asked to be a standing partner rather than a one-off seller. *** THE NAME IS NOT GIVEN. It is the player's to choose and it is a real choice -- Rowe minds the beasts and cannot read; Coll runs the barn and the basecamp and HAS HIS AUTHORITY IN WRITING (articles.md).

*** THE NAME IS COLL, AND IT CLOSES L058. *** Tristle: 'Coll runs our camp - you can trust him. We'll come by here and check whenever we're up at the crag.' *** COLL IS THE STRONGEST ANSWER THE PARTY HAD AND IT IS NOT A CONVENIENT ONE: nine years on Rell's ground, runs the barn AND the basecamp, built the spring and the lean-to, and ALREADY HOLDS HIS AUTHORITY IN WRITING (articles.md) -- the party wrote that down before any of this. Naming him costs nothing new in trust because the trust was already documented. *** AND THE SECOND HALF OF TRISTLE'S SENTENCE IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT WORK BOTH WAYS: 'we'll come by here and check whenever we're up at the crag'. That is the party taking on the CHECKING, not just the leaving -- which is what turns a drop-box into a channel. Durnhak asked for a name; Tristle gave him a name AND a habit. *** WHAT IT COSTS: Coll now has to be told there are gnomes under the hill. He is the first person outside the party to know it.

column7: 1 (no Sarn), 1 (Wend not asked about the kettle), 5 (the selling went well), 4d10+100=117 gp, 2 (Mund took the lot)
column8: *** THE CATCH-UP IN WETHERSBY, DUSK OF THE 102nd, AND HASK'S HALF OF IT IS TWO INSTRUCTIONS DISOBEYED AND A GOOD PRICE. *** HE SOLD THE WHOLE LOT TO MUND THE SMITH AT THE DAY-100 MARKET FOR 117 GOLD (4d10+100; d6=5, it went well and one buyer took everything). 421 lb out of areas 13 and 18 plus the entire kitchen haul -- chain, thirteen shovels, the smith's kit, the vise, fifteen chisels, two trade toolboxes, the bellows, sixty unfletched arrows, thirteen pots and pans, the sheave block AND THE KETTLE. *** (1) d6=1: HE DID NOT ASK COLL FOR SARN. He sold it out of his head, and HE CANNOT READ OR RECKON -- which the party knew, which is precisely why the clerk was named. There is NO ITEMISED RECORD and there never will be: he has the money and the buyer's name and nothing else. *** (2) d6=1: HE DID NOT ASK WEND ABOUT THE KETTLE. It went with the lot. He was told plainly to ask first and hold it aside if she said so. *** THIS IS NOT THEFT AND NOT MALICE AND THE MONEY IS RIGHT -- 117 gp, handed over whole. DAVE STOOD SURETY FOR THIS MAN PERSONALLY, with his purse and his name, and the surety is not broken. WHAT IS BROKEN IS THE PROCESS, and the first thing an unrecorded sale costs is the ability to DIVIDE it: nobody can now say what part of 117 was the kettle and what part the vise, so the xp had to go to the broadest set with a claim. *** AND THE SIXTY UNFLETCHED ARROWS WENT WITH IT -- the one item on that salvage list this party actually consumes. *** THE PARTY'S HALF OF THE CATCH-UP: the gnoll, area 12 and the library, Durnhak met face to face and paid, the channel with the slab and the cut mark, COLL NAMED AS THE CONTACT, and 29 bars of iron standing in Wethersby tonight.

column7: Hask 106 enthusiastic, Dellie and Ista 82 favourable
column8: *** THE PARTY TREATS HASK'S SALE AS A JOB DONE, SPLITS THE 117 NINE WAYS, AND TELLS THEM ABOUT THE IRON. *** Dave, on the two disobeyed instructions: 'if he sold and got it done and it's less work all around, great.' No reprimand, no lecture. The party's judgement, and defensible -- the money came over whole. *** THIRTEEN GOLD EACH, NINE WAYS, dividing exactly. Landed ENTHUSIASTIC on Hask (106) and favourable on Dellie and Ista (82) -- and the reason is in articles.md: it is a CUT OF WORK evenly stated, not a kindness offered to somebody with nothing to give back, and nobody was asked to choose in front of an audience. Gifts land badly; work lands. *** BRAND EXCLUDED AT HIS OWN TERMS: 'he signed on for no money.' He asked to be taught, not paid, and the party is holding to the bargain HE set rather than improving it for him -- which is the same instinct as not manufacturing a date for Orm's wage. He keeps his half share of experience. *** TOLD TO HASK AND DELLIE: the gnoll, area 12 and the library, the half-ellipse corridor, DURNHAK MET FACE TO FACE AND PAID -- 32 gp 4 sp in stores and 4 gp 6 sp in coin against the 37 Tristle named him -- the channel with the slab and the cut mark at the watercourse, COLL NAMED AS THE CONTACT, and the west waste that cost them a day. *** AND THE PLAN: 29 BARS TO MUND. He took the whole salvage lot for 117 without blinking and he is the town's smith. About 37 gp 5 sp of whatever the bars make is Durnhak's the moment they sell.

column7: reaction 84+15=99, 4 (he raises the board plainly), 5 (wants the wire), 2d10+90=99 gp iron, 2d4=5 gp wire
column8: *** MUND, SECOND DEALING, REACTION 99 -- and he is delighted, because he has just had 117 gp of their salvage and it was good. *** THEN HE MAKES THE ARGUMENT THE PARTY BUILT FOR HIM (d6=4, he says it plainly rather than just offering low): THEIR OWN AT-COST BOARD. *** The party sells iron, nails and salt AT COST, on a public board, in this hundred, as policy. assets.tsv prices a comparable 600 lb load at 100 gp AT LUDBURY -- and the board sells at the LUDBURY price, which is exactly why 'at cost' has been running 50-70 gp BELOW cost (articles.md's fourth finding, which the party found itself). *** SO HE ASKS, REASONABLY, WHY HE SHOULD PAY MORE FOR BAR IRON THAN THE PARTY'S OWN BOARD ASKS. There is no answer to that which the party has not already published. *** ⚠ NOTHING HERE TOUCHES THE SEALED d6=6. Knowing the board's price is not admitting he buys off it in quantity, and the board is nailed up in public. *** HIS OFFER: 99 GP FOR THE 29 BARS (2d10+90 -- essentially the board rate, with a little for 609 lb standing in front of him today in one lot instead of waiting on a Ludbury run) AND 5 GP FOR THE TWENTY FEET OF COPPER WIRE, which he wants (d6=5) because fine drawn wire is LABOUR not material and nobody in the north hundred draws it. 104 gp the two. *** AND THE CONSEQUENCE THE PARTY MUST BE TOLD: half of what the iron makes is Durnhak's. At 99 that is 49 gp 5 sp, NOT the ~75 the estimate carried. He has already had 37 -- so he is owed 12 gp 5 sp, not 37 gp 5 sp. TRISTLE'S OVER-GENEROUS 37 UP FRONT TURNS OUT TO BE THREE QUARTERS OF HIS ENTIRE HALF. *** NO SALE LOGGED. The offer is on the bench and the decision is the player's.

*** THE IRON BOARD WAS REPRICED, BACKFILLED HERE BECAUSE IT HAPPENED AND WAS NEVER LOGGED. *** Player, day 102: 'Since we agreed with Wend about the new price, it is done. We agreed we weren't going to be involved in the details anymore, so this is a detail that happened.' *** CONSISTENT WITH THE RECORD IN THREE PLACES and not a retcon of convenience: (1) DAY 77, the fourth finding, DECIDED -- 'price the NEW properly and SHOW THE ROAD IN THE PRICE. Do not reprice the old.' (2) DAY 92, the two numbers in hand for the FIRST time -- Tam's Marchford price list unasked, plus what it cost to fetch -- and the L024 note says in as many words 'WHY IT CAN GO UP NOW'. (3) DAY 94, 'WEND HAS THE BOARD TO PUT UP, four letters out to holders.' *** AND THE DELEGATION IS ITSELF ON THE RECORD: Dave, day 96, 'we trust you run the business.' The party handed Wend the trade and stopped auditing her details, which is exactly why a board going up generates no scene. *** WHAT IT NOW SHOWS: the road in the price. ONE NUMBER BECAME TWO -- what it cost at Ludbury and what it cost to fetch -- so a comparable 600 lb of iron reads at its LAID-DOWN ~160 gp and not the 100 Ludbury price it carried before. The day-20 gift stock is NOT repriced, per the finding's own instruction. *** MY FAILURE AND NOT THE PARTY'S: the decision, the numbers and the board are all in the log and the moment it went up is not. A DELEGATED ACT STILL NEEDS A ROW.

column7: 5 (says more than he means to), 2d10+135=146 gp
column8: *** THE MUND NEGOTIATION REDONE AGAINST THE REPRICED BOARD. THE OLD ROLLS ARE VOID: d6=4 'points at the board and asks why he should pay more' and 2d10+90 = 99 gp both rested on a board reading ~100 for 600 lb, and it reads ~160 LAID DOWN. HIS OWN SENTENCE NOW ARGUES FOR THE HIGHER NUMBER. *** KEPT: reaction 99, and that he wants the copper wire at 5 gp -- neither depended on the board. *** HIS OFFER: 146 GP FOR THE 29 BARS and 5 for the wire, 151 the two. That is a modest discount off his own alternative cost of ~160, for taking 609 lb in one lot today with no waiting on a Ludbury run -- and he is not a grinder; two days ago he took the whole salvage lot at 117 without haggling. *** d6=5, HE SAYS MORE THAN HE MEANS TO: he lets out that he BUYS IRON OFF THE PARTY'S OWN BOARD, and a good deal of it, and that the board going up has been felt. *** THAT IS A LEGITIMATE REVEAL AND NOT A LEAK -- the die was rolled on how open he is, the context is a negotiation about iron prices, and THE PARTY CAUSED IT by repricing the board. What he does NOT say is that he sells it on worked at a margin. That inference is one step away and it is theirs: he is a smith, he buys their bar, and he sold them 200 finished spikes on the 97th. *** AND DURNHAK'S HALF COMES OUT AT 73 GP against the ~75 Tristle named him down a shaft. The estimate was good to a gold and a half. He has had 37; THIRTY-SIX IS OWED once this sells.

*** DAVE RUNS THE WHOLE HAUL PAST TOLLER AT HIS MARKET PITCH, day 121, with the two laden horses (d100=67, warm and helpful). *** What Dave laid out: the meeting room and the fungus garden, the sixty labelled casks and barrels (a letter code on each; SD is the ale Holt named), the plain gold ring and the silver bracelet, the supply room (nails, mortar, hardware, spikes, rope, eighty ten-foot beams, four hundred stone blocks, six doors), the orc and troglodyte gear at the basecamp, the five sealed casks on the horses. TOLLER'S ADVICE: (1) FOOD IS NOT HIS LINE; a sealed cask sells by what is in it and a letter does not tell him that. A letter code is a STOREMAN'S code, made so somebody could find things. Ask Holt, who read SD off a bung; open one of each mark in front of a buyer and TASTE it, and do not sell what you have not tasted. (2) THE RING AND THE BRACELET: he weighed them in his palm and will buy at full value, about ten gold for the ring by weight and eight for the bracelet; no offer pressed. (3) TIMBER, DRY AND DRESSED, IS A JOINER'S TRADE: tell Bern before anybody else. (4) STONE BLOCKS AND THE DOORS are heavy and cheap; leave them unless a use turns up. (5) He would not carry more casks to town for the party without knowing what is in them. NOTHING WAS SOLD OR DECIDED.

*** CORRECTION TO SCENE 121:1, PLAYER-CAUGHT: THERE IS NO REACTION ROLL FOR TOLLER. *** He is an established NPC, not a first contact (PHB p.63 is a first-contact mechanic; log.py's own help says most scenes have none). The d100=67 in 121:1 is VOID and its 'reaction 67' figure is struck; Toller's warm, honest stance comes from the record (days 55, 65, 83, 93, 96, 100), not from a die. THE CONTENT OF HIS ADVICE STANDS: it was authored from his character, not from the number.

*** SECOND CORRECTION TO SCENE 121:1, PLAYER-CAUGHT. *** (1) TOLLER DID NOT HANDLE THE RING: the party will not let anyone touch it while it may be magical, so he was told of it and never weighed it and made no offer; the ring stays in its sack. (2) THE ORC AND TROGLODYTE GEAR WAS BROUGHT ALONG: the player said on day 120 to load as much as could safely be carried and the whole basecamp stash rode the two horses (a retcon of my mis-scoped load). (3) THE BERSERKER'S BROAD SWORD WAS PICKED UP (a retcon: he meant to). WHAT HAPPENED NEXT: Dave offers Toller the SILVER BRACELET and any of the orc gear. TOLLER BUYS THE BRACELET at full value, 8 gp. He is not interested in the weapons: he is a book and curio man, not an armourer; Mund the smith is the man for axes, heads and bows, and the market for the rest. Nothing else sold.

*** DAVE TELLS MUND WHAT THEY FOUND, day 121, at his forge with the two laden horses. NO REACTION ROLL: Mund is a known NPC (days 97, 102). *** Dave said the party keeps its spikes but would sell them if he needed them, and asked what else he wants. MUND'S INTEREST, from his trade (iron and worked iron) at the campaign's rate of HALF THE PHB LIST for used arms (rules/equipment.md): six hand axes 5 sp each = 3 gp; the berserker's broad sword 5 gp; the pair of light crossbows 6 gp each = 12 gp (he wants the lockwork and the iron); the two polearm heads, which he names as voulges (list 5 gp), 2 gp 5 sp each = 5 gp; the orc spear, 5 sp. NOT HIS TRADE: the short bow (a bowyer's) and rope. THE HARDWARE BOX: he would take it, to sort by the piece, at about 20 gp, more if there is a good lock in it -- a DM call, flagged, no PHB price. The spikes: he would make more at the day-97 price if the party ever wants them; no offer on these. NOTHING SOLD YET: the party decides.

*** THE FIVE CASKS OPENED AT THE INN WITH HOLT, day 121. NO REACTION ROLL (known NPC). *** B = wheat flour (~14 lb), LC = salt (~30 lb), QS = seasoning, dried herbs and spice (~8 lb), RH = sunflower seeds (~10 lb), VW = lard (~23 lb); all stale but sound, the module's off-taste. TRUE WEIGHTS with the ~10 lb cask: 24, 40, 18, 20 and 33 lb, replacing my 40 lb liquid-equivalent guess. HOLT'S DECISION, from his trade, offers DM-call priced against the PHB food list (no book prices bulk goods): flour 7 sp, salt 6 gp, lard 2 gp 3 sp, seasoning 2 gp 4 sp = 11 gp 4 sp; he passes on the seeds (nobody pays for those). NOTHING SOLD YET. THE ALE: the party says there is more SD in the dungeon (three containers counted, one barrel and two kilderkins). Holt is keen, at the day-71 rate: 58 gp a full barrel (36 gallons), 29 a kilderkin (18): 116 gp for the three, on delivery. He also raises L010: the 28 gp he still owes from the first barrel, to be set against the next; NOT PAID, LOOP STAYS OPEN.

*** FOUR CASKS SOLD TO HOLT AT HIS PRICES, day 121: 11 gp 4 sp (flour 7 sp, salt 6 gp, lard 2 gp 3 sp, seasoning 2 gp 4 sp). NO REACTION ROLL. The seed cask resealed and kept. DAVE TELLS HOLT THERE IS A LOT MORE IN THE DUNGEON, IN FULL-SIZED BARRELS, and asks if he wants it. HOLT'S TERMS at the same per-pound rate as the casks (DM calls, flagged): a barrel of flour about 8 gp 4 sp, of salt about 72 gp, of lard about 27 gp 6 sp; ale 58 gp a barrel and 29 a kilderkin. HIS LIMIT is what an inn can use in a season, not what a cellar can hold: at most two barrels of flour, two of salt, one of lard, a firkin's worth of seasoning, and ALL the ale that comes; he takes nothing whose contents he has not seen; bring him the marks nobody knows and he will open one of each and say. Nothing agreed to be hauled yet.

*** DAVE TELLS WEND EVERYTHING FROM LUDBURY'S RUMOUR CONVERSATIONS, day 121, at the barn. NO REACTION ROLL (known NPC). *** WHAT SHE HEARD, from transcript lines 51641-51811 (day 108): the rumour on the Ludbury wool market is that the party's floor is too low because it does not pay for hauling, when the party hauls its own; it is WIDESPREAD; NOBODY CAN NAME WHERE IT STARTED; asked straight, no trader could say who is being shorted or by whom -- it reads as a SENTENCE PEOPLE REPEAT, not a grievance with a holder's name on it; the party told the traders it bought at the floor and gave each holder a real share of the profit, several reconsidered and one said it was the first he had heard of it done so; it starves the rumour a little and produced no name. THE MARKET: raw fleece about 26 gp a tod (she already knew, from the sale), and SORTED AND GRADED wool about a third more, 34-35 gp, which she did NOT have. WEND'S READING (authored from her character, not rolled): a rumour that survives on repetition and not substance was PUT INTO CIRCULATION by somebody who gains if the holders stop trusting the floor -- a buyer who would rather bid against a floor nobody believes in, or a man with a quarrel with the venture -- but she names nobody and will not guess a name aloud. HER PLAN: when the four holders' answers to her letters come back (L043, before shearing) she will add to each reply one plain question -- has he heard the hauling complaint, and from whom -- because if holders have heard it, they heard it from somebody. She will also look at grading the district's wool at home before selling raw, since a third more is worth the work. NOTHING DECIDED BY THE PARTY.

*** DAVE ASKS WEND FOR THE CARTS AND ABOUT THE ROPE AND MORTAR, day 121. NO REACTION ROLL (known NPC). *** (1) THE THREE CARTS AND THEIR MULES, to go up to the crag tomorrow once market day is done, for more supplies: the party's own TWO carts and two mules, and HALM'S OWN cart and mule (the mule the party bought him after Hask's crew robbed him; the player, day 121). WEND SAYS YES to the party's two; HALM'S IS HIS, so she will ask him tonight, and expects him to jump: he is the carter who asked for a run once, on day 40, and said he would not ask twice. She will settle a fair day's hire for himself, cart and mule with him and write it down; she has worked with him often. Nothing agreed with Halm yet. (2) THE HEAVY 200-FT ROPE AND THE MORTAR: her answer, from her character, is COLL, who runs the barn and the basecamp and built the spring and the lean-to nobody asked for; a builder wants both and would trade a favour, not coin. She suggests taking them up in the carts tomorrow and offering them to him there, not selling them in town where nobody wants a nearly empty sack of mortar. NOTHING SOLD, NOTHING DECIDED.

*** CORRECTION TO SCENE 121:8, PLAYER-CAUGHT: COLL IS NEVER AT THE BASECAMP -- he only built it for the party. *** Wend's suggestion to take the rope and mortar up to the crag and offer them to him there was mine and it was wrong. WHAT HAPPENED: Dave says they will tell Coll the rope and mortar are in the barn if he has a use for them; Wend says she will tell him herself, he is in and out of the barn. Dave thanks her and the two go back to the Inn. NOTHING SOLD, NOTHING DECIDED.

*** DAVE ASKS COLL WHETHER TO BUILD A BETTER PATH UP TO THE CAVES OR KEEP BRINGING THE BIG BARRELS DOWN ONE AT A TIME, day 121 night, at the barn. NO REACTION ROLL (known NPC; hireling of nine years, runs the barn and the camp). *** Dave tells him there are many more barrels in the caves: sixty-odd containers, thirty-three of them full-size 36-gallon barrels at about 460 lb, sixteen kilderkins and a few smaller. COLL'S ADVICE, from his trade (DM calls, flagged, no book prices any of it): (1) THE HALF HOUR OF UNMADE OUTCROP between the basecamp and the cave mouth is what stops a cart, and a made cart road up it is a summer's work that the frost lifts, and is not worth it for barrels. (2) WHAT IS WORTH BUILDING is a SLEDGE-WAY: a cleared, graded line up the outcrop with a stout post and a brake rope at the steep pitch, so that four men and a barrel on a sledge come down under control instead of being tapped and eased off the crag one at a time. About six of his men for about eight days, at a few silver pieces a man a day, so ten gold or so of wages, and a barrel of the ale pays that back on its own. (3) HE WANTS TO SEE IT FIRST: he will walk the line with the party before he says a price, and WOULD START WITH THE STEEP PITCH. (4) FROST: it should be done before the first hard frost, which the district reckons in a few weeks. NOTHING DECIDED; he is not taking the job until asked.

*** THE PARTY ASKS COLL TO BUILD THE SLEDGE-WAY AND ASKS WHEN, day 121 night. NO REACTION ROLL. *** COLL'S TERMS (DM calls, flagged): he will come up with the carts in the morning and walk the outcrop from the basecamp to the cave mouth on the day after they arrive (day 123), and START THE SAME DAY with SIX HANDS he can have at the camp by then, from his own roll. EIGHT WORKING DAYS, TEN IF THE WEATHER TURNS, so the sledge-way is ready by about day 131, at the outside day 133, before the first hard frost. The steep pitch first, so it can be used as soon as it stands. WAGES about ten gold in all, PAID TO COLL ON COMPLETION, the barrels coming down the old way in the meantime. NOTHING SIGNED; the party said yes.

*** CORRECTION TO SCENES 121:5 AND 121:6, THE PLAYER'S DIRECTION: HOLT'S PRICES WERE TOO HIGH AND ARE REPRICED. *** The four casks realised 1.71 gp at the corrected price board (rules/prices.md, day 121: flour 2 cp/lb, lard 4, salt 8, seasoning 12, stale factor 0.75), not 11 gp 4 sp; the difference, 9.69 gp, is taken back in money.tsv and 10 xp in encounters.tsv. HOLT'S BARREL QUOTES at the same scale, stale: flour about 1 gp 5 sp a barrel (168 lb), salt about 10 gp 16 sp, lard about 4 gp 3 sp; all far below the quotes in 121:6. THE ALE IS NOT SETTLED: see the price question raised in reply.

THE MEAL AT COLL'S BASECAMP, day 122 dusk, with Coll in it. Ista directs the cooking of the camp food and Dave enforces her orders; over the meal Dave announces that tonight the party spends the night at Coll's basecamp WITH COLL, and capers a jig round the fire. No reaction roll (known NPCs); colour only, nothing mechanical.

DINNER AT COLL'S BASECAMP, day 123 evening, and DAVE'S DANCE IN HONOUR OF COLL. Torsat, Tristle and Frython take up a beat and a hum, arranged beforehand; Dave dances the Irish step dance by the fire, 'Tonight, in honor of Coll!'. No reaction roll (known NPCs); colour only, nothing mechanical.

DINNER AT COLL'S BASECAMP, day 124 evening, Ista cooking again, and TRISTLE'S BALLET IN HONOUR OF COLL: graceful, elven; Dave and Torsat hum somberly at first and then increasingly sillily. Same day the player said the wages are paid in full for the promised seven days, not shortened by the party's help (loop L062). No reaction roll (known NPCs); colour only.

DAVE ASKS COLL, over dinner, day 125: since the sledge-way will stand early, could the crew stay and help get the barrels down to the basecamp? COLL SAYS YES: the days you have paid for are paid, so the men haul on the days the road saves, no charge; days past the seven are the same rate; his hands work the OUTCROP, from the cave mouth down, and NOT down the hole (day-11 promise). The party rolls the barrels to the cave mouth. No reaction roll (known NPC).

DAVE ASKS COLL, over dinner, day 126: could the party improvise a sledge or two from the trees so it can help haul? COLL SAYS YES: green poles from the stand below the camp, where the lean-to's poles came from; runners, cross-bearers, lashed with the party's ropes; two rough ones by mid-morning tomorrow, cut at first light by the hands. He wants the party's three ropes and the crosscut saw from the lean-to. Both new sledges need four men each, which is the party's. No reaction roll (known NPC).

DAVE THANKS THE CREW AT THE END OF THE HAULING, day 127 dinner: 'That was some mighty fine work! ... we appreciate you staying and helping with the barrels.' one gold piece to each of the six hands, to Rowe and to Orm and two to Coll, ten in all from the purse (audit-skip), on top of the promised wages. Framed as pay for extra work done, not a gift: the work-lands rule (articles.md). Then 'Now let's celebrate the end of a job well done! Who's up for a dance?' No reaction roll (known NPCs); colour only.

DAY 129 MORNING: THE TRIO CHECK IN WITH TOLLER AT HIS PITCH and sell him the plain gold ring at full value, 10 gp, as with the bracelet. Dave tells him the barrels are down and sealed and that the casks and marks (L050) will be opened in their turn. No reaction roll (known NPC); colour only.
DAY 129 LATE MORNING: THE TRIO SELL MUND THE TWO BERSERKER SWORDS at half list, the used-arms rate: the broad sword 5 gp, the long sword 7 gp 10 sp. No reaction roll (known NPC); colour only.

THE PARTY ASKS HALM TO COME UP TO THE CRAG, day 130 evening, in person, at his yard in Wethersby: cart and mule to the basecamp at first light on day 131 to carry the rest of the barrels, 8 sp a day (5 sp teamster, DMG p.28, and 3 sp for the mule, rules/prices.md). HE SAYS YES AT ONCE: he is the carter who wants a run and asked once, on day 40, and said he would not ask twice; asked to his face, it lands as work. Wend to write it down at the barn in the morning. Hire owed on return. No reaction roll (known NPC).

DAVE ASKS HOLT, day 134 evening at the Inn, whether he will come to Wend's barn to open and buy some of the new barrels the party has brought down. HOLT SAYS HE WILL COME: after the morning rush tomorrow. He has bought from the party before (four casks, the SD ale on a profit share, L010: he still owes 28 gp). No reaction roll (known NPC); colour only.

DAVE ASKS HOLT HOW HE WANTS TO PAY for the sound goods in the barn (419 gp at the day-135 prices), regular payments or some other system. HOLT'S TWO OFFERS, authored from the record (a publican with thin coin, L010: he owes 28 gp on the day-71 ale): fifty gold now, the most in the till; then EITHER a TAB at the Inn against the party's board and ale (the party's board is 10 gp a night for ten), which also wipes out the 28 gp he owes, OR thirty gold in coin every market day as the barrels sell until it is done. NOTHING DECIDED YET. No reaction roll (known NPC).

DAVE TELLS COLL, at the barn, day 135: the heavy rope (200 ft) and the bag of mortar are his to use as he sees fit; and asks whether he needs the barrels of water. COLL TAKES THE ROPE AND THE MORTAR (a wall at the barn wants pointing before the frost; work tools, not a kindness, so it lands); the WATER: NO, the barn has its own well; tip it in the yard trough, and the party keeps the barrels. No reaction roll (known NPC).

DAY 135 AFTERNOON, THE TRIO SELL THE LAST ODDS AND ENDS: TOLLER takes the silver-plated comb (5 gp), the small tapestry (40 gp) and the two half-full perfume bottles (3 gp each) at full value, 51 gp in coin; HOLT takes the small keg with spigot and gimlet, 1 gp on the account; MUND takes the gnoll's morning star and the gnoll-sized sword as iron, 2 gp 10 sp each, 5 gp. The water in the OG containers tipped into Wend's trough at Coll's word. No reaction roll (known NPCs).

DAY 135 LATE AFTERNOON, THE TRIO AT WEND'S FOR NEWS: (1) L043: ONE OF THE FOUR HOLDERS, ELLERY, HAS ANSWERED, understood floor and share, heard the low-floor rumour and did not credit it; three answers still out. (2) L039: OSK SAYS YES to the cart-hire sheet, 5 sp a day the cart with its mule on the road, nothing on days it stands, his name on the contract; Wend has drafted it and holds it unsigned for the party. (3) L047: NOTHING NEW on who in Ludbury. The party checks in with Wend for news, day 141. Dave suggests finding an actual druid Brand could talk to, rather than deciding on secondhand description alone. Nobody in the party knows of one nearby -- genuinely open question, who to ask is undecided.

Dave asks Ossery, delicately, whether he knows anyone in Marchford or Ludbury he'd quietly arrange with to make warehouse/barn theft stop -- not the watch. Ossery, known NPC, no reaction rolled (settled disposition). If it exists anywhere formally, it would be Ludbury, a real city -- but that's not his trade and he has no name to give. Asks, with real concern, whether the party is having trouble of its own.

Dave levels with Ossery: no trouble, and the party's real trade is adventuring, not wool -- cave work, where moving quiet and staying out of torchlight matters. Ossery visibly recalibrates (hadn't known; the party's known to Marchford only through goods and the correspondent arrangement). Rolled d6=5 against a 1-2 threshold for whether he personally knows anyone who teaches that -- no, genuinely doesn't, mercers don't go underground. But he redirects usefully: the men who guard the caravans on the road through the hills do that kind of work for a living, and he'd ask them before he asked anyone else, though he can't promise anything -- he names no one specific.

A caravan guard, enthusiastically friendly (d100=97) about helping, calls out to his company's scout HULME by name and trade in front of the others -- 'these folks are asking about your OTHER work.' Hulme's reaction to actually being asked, d100=19, hostile. He goes cold, denies everything flatly, and is visibly furious at being named out loud in front of men he works with -- being known as a thief, even a retired/working one, is not safe for a man whose job depends on being trusted with a caravan's goods. He does not attack; this is a trade town and there is no cause, but the conversation is over and he will not be approached again today.

Dave apologises to Caddow for the awkward spot and offers coin for two drinks, himself and Hulme, to make up for it -- 1 gp. Established NPC now (first contact already rolled this scene), no new reaction roll. Caddow accepts gratefully and visibly relieved Dave isn't sore at him; says he'll make sure Hulme isn't sour about it by nightfall. No promise of anything further from Hulme today.

Tristle approaches Hulme alone, quietly, while he's mending a strap by the second wagon -- no naming, no audience. Opens in Thieves' Cant (PHB p.26, automatic to all thieves regardless of alignment) rather than saying anything aloud about trade. Continuing an established NPC arc (Caddow's overnight smoothing, d6=5 on the 144/145 boundary), not a fresh first-contact roll -- his guard visibly drops the instant he recognises it; cant can't be faked, so it's proof in a way words from a stranger weren't. Genuine, cautious conversation opens. Not yet resolved: terms, price, whether he can actually get free of his caravan contract to do it.

Before riding for Ludbury, the trio asks Ossery what wool is fetching. Known NPC, no reaction roll. Rolled for price movement same procedure as day 108's check (then ~26 gp/tod, Ludbury): d6=3, about the same since. An evening touring taverns, listening only, not asking. Nobody at the table laughs. The subject changes fast. No name given for anything, no new NPC met -- pure atmosphere confirming something organized plausibly operates here, not a lead to follow yet.

Morning at the wool market -- asked several dealers for a range, not just one figure. Grade matters more than anyone's haggling: raw/unsorted running 15-18 gp/tod, clean graded wool up around 30-32, the ~26 gp/tod figure from yesterday sitting as the typical middle for ordinary good wool. The party's own art.7 floor (8 gp/tod) is well under even the LOW end. Continued listening for guild talk alongside it -- rolled d6=3 (declared 1-3 nothing new, 4-5 small texture, 6 something new): nothing new today, same wariness whenever the subject brushes close, no fresh detail.

Dave recalls Toller already has a correspondent here -- DARROW, the dealer from day 86 who wanted access to Sir Aymer's hall (interactions.tsv 86:2, L008) and was never personally named until now. Also asked whether he's heard of Rogahn and Zelligar -- not DM-spoiler content, these are the party's own long-established findings (the crag's builders, per the lord's charter day 51 and Zelligar's diary/headboard/plaque still with Toller). Rolled d6=3 (declared 1-2 only vague legend, 3-4 trade gossip -- a Zelligar-attributed diary has apparently surfaced somewhere, people have been asking; 5-6 something more concrete): Darrow's heard the names because of trade gossip -- word that a diary attributed to Zelligar has surfaced, and that people have been asking after it. He doesn't know it's the party's own diary, sitting with Toller on open terms, unsold. Nothing further -- he can't say who's asking or why, just that it's being talked about.

Asked Darrow plainly what roads leave Ludbury and where they go. He mentions, as a matter of ordinary trade knowledge not a secret, that it's the road Sir Aymer's own wool has come down these two summers. THIS ANSWERS THE OLD DAY-6 QUESTION'S OTHER HALF: the party has known since Cuddy that Sir Aymer simply never thought of Wethersby (d6=3, no scheme) -- this is the first time anyone has told them the actual route his clip takes. Logged to knowledge.tsv as 'draycot_south', known.

Dave asks if Darrow knows any dealers in Wraye -- the one town where Toller's six-correspondents network (L008) still has nobody. Darrow's honest about it -- Wraye's a library town, scholars and students, not much trade passes through worth a Ludbury dealer's notice. He's never had reason to deal there.

A general wander, listening for whatever's being talked about, no particular subject. More wandering, listening. Vague, uncertain, the way travelers' gossip usually is -- not actionable.
Last day before the Hulme rendezvous, more wandering, listening. Rolled d6=5, minor color only: nothing beyond the ordinary texture of a market city going about its day.

The informal evening assessment, at camp. Tristle asks directly about Ludbury's Thieves' Guild. Confirms yes, Ludbury has one, and Merrick's situation -- selective, light-touch break-ins as a warning rather than real theft -- matches exactly how such outfits keep a target compliant without drawing the watch's attention: take little or nothing, just prove they can get in, so the next visit (the real one, if it ever comes) is understood. He will NOT give the name tonight -- not a refusal, just plain that it's a bigger thing than three days of trust covers, and asks to be asked again once there's more reason to.

Second evening on the road, more informal practice -- no fresh percentage rolls (that was the baseline test, day 150), just coaching and repetition on the same weak points (moving quiet, staying unseen). Montage pace, not mechanically resolved tonight.

While Tristle trains, Dave and Blartho spend downtime testing the unidentified plain metal ring (L029, area 27 dais) by trial and error -- sparring with wooden sticks, trading the ring back and forth, checking for effects on attacking, being hit, hiding, and strength/speed. (2) BEING HIT: real, simulated with actual dice -- 40 sparring exchanges, Dave attacking Blartho, 20 with the ring on Blartho and 20 without, same conditions otherwise. Without: 14/20 hits (70%). With: 9/20 hits (45%). A clear, consistent swing in the same direction every time it was tried -- Blartho noticeably harder to connect with while wearing it. (3) HIDING/VISIBILITY: no detectable difference. (4) STRENGTH/SPEED: no detectable difference, no change in what either could lift or how fast they moved. Functional conclusion available to the characters: wearing it seems to make the wearer harder to hit in melee, nothing else detected. They do not have precise certainty of the exact bonus from 40 trials, only that the effect is real and one-directional.

Dave and Blartho ride the circuit around Marchford from outside, a perspective they haven't had (day 144's visit was all from inside the town). More specific flood news, closer to the source than Ludbury's secondhand version day 147. Rolled d6=3 (declared 1-2 minor, 3-4 serious and resolved, 5-6 ongoing/worse): a village upstream lost livestock and stored grain over several weeks of high water, bad enough that it's real news here, not idle talk -- but it's over now, which matches the bridge's own repair work being done rather than in progress. No name given for the village; not pursued further, just fuller context on the rumor already noted.

A week's uninterrupted training complete (DMG p.86), final 750 gp paid. Hulme confirms it plainly rather than making a ceremony of it -- Tristle leveled, 2nd, hp roll 5 (3->8 max). XP freeze lifted -- earns normally toward 2,501 (3rd) from here. Per PHB's own rule, every lock/trap he was previously STUMPED on may be tried again: Open Locks at (6,16,H), Find/Remove Traps on the area-13 statue at (3,19), and the area 36 pit trap at (29,31)/(29,30) that's sat jammed-open since day 46. Yrtone and Torsat arrive at Draycot, day 145, the end of the two-day walk from Wethersby. Cuddy receives them warmly, established NPC, no reaction roll. Yrtone gives Wilfred the full, accurate account. GHOULS: two, area 22 the Garden Room, day 119 expedition 16 -- both shot dead at range before either could close, no paralysis, no casualties; Yrtone's own turn attempt against the first failed (11 vs 16). Both stocked ghouls confirmed dead; nothing says whether more exist elsewhere in the unexplored dungeon. Wilfred writes all of it down, visibly more concerned at the second kind -- two separate sources of undead in the same place, not one. Scene open for his follow-up.

Yrtone, honestly: no sign of a cause, nothing found despite repeated trips in and out, and level 2 isn't fully explored yet. Wilfred accepts it plainly -- asks for nothing more invented, writes the limit down as part of the account rather than pressing for an answer that doesn't exist. Says he'll carry it back to his house as it stands and asks, before anything else, that word be sent if the party ever does find a cause. Interview concluded for now.

Two questions put to Cuddy directly. DRUID: rolled d6=3 (declared 1-2 no, 3-4 heard secondhand, 5-6 knows personally), then d6=5 for how current (declared 1-2 old story, 3-4 a specific avoided place, 5-6 recent, within a year or two): he's heard something, recent enough to be real -- talk of someone seen in a patch of old woodland somewhere in the hundred, within the last year or so. No name, no personal contact, just that it's recent and the kind of thing people say carefully. ROOF: Ottir's own day-77 advice, finally asked. Rolled d6=2 (declared 1-2 yes clearly) -- Cuddy remembers plainly: a local man, STENNET, mended it roughly twelve years back (d6=3-4 band), paid for by a couple of villagers as a kindness, nothing to do with the hall. Directly useful to the custom question: the roof has never once been the hall's business.

BACKFILLED, player-flagged gap: the standing intent was for Dave/Tristle/Blartho to keep asking about a druid throughout their travels, not just the one Marchford attempt (day 144, negative) -- never explicitly re-raised during the 5+ days in Ludbury. Rolled now rather than left silently unresolved: d6=6 (declared 1-3 nothing, 4-5 a fragment similar to Cuddy's, 6 something more specific), then d6=3 for the content (a secondhand description of the person) and d6=2 for specifics: someone in Ludbury's market recalled, offhand, an old man seen out in rough country somewhere in the district -- plainly dressed, moved oddly sure-footed for his age, nothing else remembered clearly. No name, no precise place. Complements rather than confirms Cuddy's own answer (145:7) -- same general shape (a figure seen in the countryside, recent), independent source.

Yrtone asks where to find Stennet. Rolled d6=1 (declared 1-2 gone) then d6=5 (declared 4-5 moved away to a bigger town, unclear if still alive): Cuddy doesn't know where he is now, only that he left the village some years back for a bigger town -- can't say which, can't say if he's even living. The historical fact (who, roughly when, paid by villagers not the hall) stands regardless; the man himself isn't easily found. Separately, asked what town Wilfred's own house is in: rolled d6=2 (declared 1-2 Ludbury) -- LUDBURY, the same city that retains Neot (L056), a real, existing religious institution already on the party's own map, not a new unplaced location.

Asked if anyone local could actually do the roof now that Stennet's gone. Rolled d6=4 (declared 1-2 nobody, 3-4 someone competent, 5-6 well-regarded) -- yes, ALRIC (d6=3), capable, not a master but up to a straightforward repair. Rolled whether he's actually around to ask today: d6=1 (declared 1-2 away at work elsewhere) -- not in the village, out working somewhere else, can't be met on this visit. Named, but not reachable today; the party's own fallback (send a crew down from Wethersby, already the day-135 plan with Coll, ~30 gp ceiling per L016) stands as the practical option.
